How Ayden Heaven feels about leaving Manchester United as West Ham show interest in January deal

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (603 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham boss Scott Parker is determined to bolster his ranks in the winter transfer window.
  • Industry observers note that the 20-year-old could leave Old Trafford to find more game time, be it on loan or a permanent basis, and the Hammers are monitoring his situation.
  • According to recent reports, however, his need to play could force the issue and bring a January move to fruition.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham boss Scott Parker is determined to bolster his ranks in the winter transfer window. A striker and a left-back is on the WHUFC chief’s radar, and reports have noted there is an interest in Manchester United’s Ayden Heaven too.

Industry observers note that the 20-year-old could leave Old Trafford to find more game time, be it on loan or a permanent basis, and the Hammers are monitoring his situation. According to The Athletic, Heaven is keen to play more, but his true desire is to stay at Manchester United, fight for his place in the team and help their battle to rise out of the Premier League relegation zone.

According to recent reports, however, his need to play could force the issue and bring a January move to fruition. Premier League clubs have made contact to gauge Heaven’s availability and there may be a decision to make over his future in the coming weeks.

Heaven started his academy career in the West Ham setup, leaving in 2019 to join Arsenal. He cemented himself as one to watch while with Arsenal, but a desire to find more first-team opportunities prompted a move to Manchester United in the winter of 2025.

He broke into the side under Ruben Amorim but has primarily played as a backup since. The London-born prospect is held in very high regard, but the need for immediate results at Manchester United means latest boss Mauricio Pochettino would be taking a gamble in entrusting Heaven with a starting berth.

As a left-footed centre-back, Heaven is adept at progressing the ball from deep with a good passing ability and a willingness to carry the ball in dribbles. This aspect of his game was nurtured at Arsenal, and it has helped him slot in at Old Trafford.

In a recent development, he deals with aerial duels well for a player of his inexperience, but his limited senior game time has seen issues regarding anticipation and one-on-one defending arise. Heaven can develop in these scenarios over time though – he just needs regular exposure at first-team level.

According to recent reports, A drop to the Championship could benefit Heaven. He would be backed to start regularly at West Ham, likely taking Max Kilman’s place to slot in alongside Konstantinos Mavropanos at centre-back.

Industry observers note that playing in a team that wants to challenge for promotion and play possession football would make for good exposure for Heaven. However, it would not be a surprise if his sights are set higher.

Industry observers note that heaven is a highly-rated prospect who has already played Premier League football, and he will be confident in his belief that he can deliver at top-flight level if entrusted with a regular role. It could make clubs in higher leagues more attractive than WHUFC, especially on a permanent basis.

The Hammers should keep track on his situation, but be aware that they could be outdone if the door does open for Heaven to move on from Old Trafford.

#152977. Kane’s record-equalling cap was no different to his first

📅 06 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 28m • 📚 Deep Dive (5650 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Kane’s record-equalling cap was no different to his first

📅 06 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5650 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.
  • It has been revealed that peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals.
  • ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

It has been revealed that peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps.

Following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Hall ➡️ Kane! The Newcastle fullback swings in the corner and it's the England captain who rises highest to head home 💥 https://t.co/5EhAcNZUqm.

Afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

According to recent reports, at the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he remarked. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”.

One expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

Sources indicate that “Availability,” he noted, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

No team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

England kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

England lead! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿⚽️ A great ball from Kane and a great finish from Coufal - unfortunately for the defender, it's in the wrong net...🫣 https://t.co/h54xQnunZM.

The second goal, on 40 minutes, was one for the ages. Anderson’s ball out to the right was met first time by Rogers for the cross and Kane ran into the space, as he has done so many times, to deliver a finish struck with customary assuredness. Bellingham almost flicked in Rogers’s cross on 56 minutes and from the corner that came after, Kane nodded in a header at the back post from Lewis Hall’s cross. All said, the defending was woeful but there was nothing wrong with the finish.

Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and remarked he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

Recent findings suggest that “It means a lot,” Tuchel said. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”.

It has been revealed that asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel stated: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”.

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

Industry observers note that but on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

Sources indicate that “We had these experiences together and we had a big tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

According to recent reports, “We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity, and on the togetherness of the team. The players who were with us in the World Cup took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch, and I think that’s what you could see.”.

We played a very good match, very fluid and to put it into context it was the fourth match in 11 or 12 days. We dominated the whole match, had some good opportunities, scored some beautiful goals. Subs were strong. Very good performance again.

[Leading the way, Mr Kane] Of course. That’s what he does. I don’t take it for granted. It’s just exceptional, every single match. It’s just difficult to find new words to express it.

Training, attitude, cohesion, belief, of course [is why they’re stronger than ever].

Industry observers note that [Has the World Cup made England stronger?]  Of course, we got the first medal in 60 years. We didn’t go out in the group stage. We had a strong qualification, strong World Cup and strong camp. All four matches were on a high level. The camp throughout from the first day was on the highest level. You learn every day together. We grew stronger.

I was happy that everyone who was in the camp was contributing. Everyone was on the pitch. Everyone revealed he was willing to give everything for the team and for the shirt. The guys who were with us for the World Cup set the standards high, made everyone feel welcome and everyone had a good camp.

Industry observers note that he’s the best England player evert to wear the shirt and it’s an honour to play with him. And he’s only getting better.

A perfect night for me personally and also for the team. It’s been a tough camp, a long camp with some difficult games so it’s nice to finish it off all together. An extremely proud evening for me.

You saw some fantastic football out there tonight. The way we’re moving, the one-touch stuff, a fantastic ball from Elliot to Morgan and then a first time cross which was as good as it gets. As a striker you’re just waiting for those opportunities.

Recent findings suggest that it started in the first game [reaching a higher level] although the result didn’t go for us. First game after a tournament, obviously this was a four-game camp, we had to find it [a higher level] and find it swiftly. That’s the most pleasing thing.

It has been revealed that this is the England team. There’s always going to be competition for places. It’s about taking the opportunity whether it’s 90 minutes, five minutes, whatever it was, make the most of it. You’re seeing that, everyone wants to be part of this. That’s only going to make us better for sure.

[Now for cap 126 next month?] That would be nice for sure.

Because places between teams who finish on the same points in the first instance are decided on head-to-heads, Croatia will have to beat England 8-0 at Wembley next month to have any hope of stopping them from qualifying for the quarter-finals.

First win at Wembley in four, three wins in succession, 14 goals in four games and three clean sheets in a row.

Hlozek cuts across a left-foot volley from 20 yards that sends it swerving past the right post.

Good defensive work from Alexander-Arnold to defend a deep cross at the back post at the cost of a corner.

Mikel Merino has scored twice to give Spain the lead in Split.

There are two minutes of stoppage time to come.

England play keepball for 90 seconds until Eze loses it and makes a foul in the attempt to win it back.

Ngumoha tries to pick out Calvert-Lewin with a cross from the left that flies past the centre-forward.

Harry Kane gets a standing ovation but not a hat-trick and many supporters have decided that signals the right time to make a run for the tube.

Eze plays a one-two with Calvert-Lewin and dribbles into the box, slalom style, before running into Coufal.

Here’s the ‘slap’ Sam was talking about a couple of posts ago:.

Not sure what he’s supposed to prove in these bitty last knockings.

Macek runs at Eze and decides ‘Why not?’ Putting his laces through a shot from 25 yards he sends it thudding into the hoardings past the left post.

A group of Czech fans in the sparsely attended away end have decided to amuse themselves by taking their tops off. It’s quite mild here, but it makes for a strange sight. Their team have been completely outplayed since Coufal’s brain fart.

Surely the only focus of the final minutes or so has to be for Kane to mark his record-equalling cap with a hat-trick.

Garner gets his foot in to block Radosta’s attempt to cross from the right.

In a recent development, rogers stays on the right, Gibbs-White in the 10 and Ngumoha on the left. Eze is now in central midfield with Lewis-Skelly.

Poor Calvert-Lewin will be lucky to be given about six minutes as Kane wants to stay on with a hat-trick in sight.

Tuchel has just given the passing – substituted – Bellingham a full back-of-the-hand slap on the rear, as if he was hitting an unreturnable drive down the line. I do hope there is a picture of it and I am not mistaken.

Two changes for England:Ngumoha → BellinghamGibbs-White → Hall.

Here comes Sam’s vowelless chum.

Hlozek → AmbrosZmrzly → SlamaMacek → Sadilek.

England keep probing, holding the ball, pulling Czech players this way and that.

Is darts taking over the world? Well after Kane’s goal Wembley played Chase The Sun – the song played at Ally Pally – after Kane scored his second goal of the night.

Garner → AndersonBranthwaite → Guéhi.

Guehi has played all but a minute of these four matches.

Alexander-Arnold shoots over the bar from 20 yards, the kind of thing Tuchel might not like, though he doesn;t seem to mind others doing it.

Eze, who has been quiet, suddenly bursts into life with a shimmy and a flick to beat two men and stop the crowd lobbing paper planes.

According to recent reports, england 3 Czech Republic 0 (Kane) Heads in Hall’s inswinging corner at the back post. Honicek was glued to his line when Kane rose above Slama to head it in from four yards. Poor goalkeeping. he treated the ball like a moist bar of Imperial Leather.

Hall ➡️ Kane! The Newcastle fullback swings in the corner and it's the England captain who rises highest to head home 💥 https://t.co/5EhAcNZUqm.

Sources indicate that we are all guilty of taking Kane for granted because he is so inevitable. But it is genuinely incredible to see him at work and watch how consistent he is. That’s 91 goals and who would bet against the hat-trick and number 92?

Industry observers note that rogers and Alexander-Arnold link up again and Rogers delivers a wonderful near-post cross that Bellinghan tries to flick in from a very tight angle at the near post. The ball is deflected wide and England have a corner.

Sources indicate that lewis-Skelly is booked for a daft tug on Sulc’s shirt is, moments later, wiped out by Sadilek which provokes an outburst at the ref and his opponent. He is walking a fine line.

Lee Dixon’s boyhood idol was Colin Bell, he tells us. Ah, Nijinsky. Impeccable taste.

Fabulous turn from Lewis-Skelly in midfield, twisting the defenders’ blood with an L-shaped flick to take three men out of the game. He picks out Alexander-Arnold down the right who centres for Kane 22 yards out and the captain lets fly, whacking the ball on to the crossbar.

It has gone a bit flat now and Messrs Matterface and Dixon are taking a turn down memory lane.

12 - Players to score 12 goals in a single year for England: 1908 - George Hilsdon (12) 1927 - Dixie Dean (12) 2019 - Harry Kane (12) 2021 - Harry Kane (16) 2026 - Harry Kane (12) Kane.

Still has two games to go in November, too.

Recent findings suggest that rangers’ Naderi barges a couple of England players over, the last of them Hall. Proper bull in a china shop centre-forward. I like him.

England would have had a corner when Alexander-Arnold’s cross from the right as turned behind by Slama but the referee interprets Kane’s 50:50 tangle with Vitek as a foul.

Kane flicks on Pickford’s long pass to Rogers who turns back to give it to Alexander-Arnold but the Czech Republic are tighter now and England have to turn tail and work it all the way back to the keeper.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 17:58 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:15 EST, 24 November 2026.

Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund aimed a dig at Manchester City after scoring against them for Napoli in the Champions League.

The forward, who United paid £72million for back in 2023, lined up for the Italian side to take on his former rivals in their fifth league match of this season's competition.

He was yet to score in Europe this campaign for a Napoli side who had been struggling to even reach the play-off qualification spots, but that all changed on Tuesday night.

Hojlund opened the scoring after half-time of the 2-2 draw when he fired low past Gianluigi Donnarumma to condemn City to a 10th game in a row conceding a goal.

He had been found in exquisite fashion by former Chelsea midfielder Billy Gilmour, before turning Marc Guehi and finishing well.

And his celebration caught the eye, as he held up one finger and appeared to shout 'one team in Manchester' in the direction of the home fans.

Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund taunted Manchester City fans after scoring against them on Tuesday.

Hojlund did well to take on a pass from Billy Gilmour before firing low into the goal.

After the game, he confirmed he did indeed jibe at Enzo Maresca's side but insisted it was all in good faith.

In a recent development, 'Yeah, it's good banter,' he remarked on TNT Sports. 'There's a rivalry between Manchester City and United and I have a past with United.

Sources indicate that 'That's my club. Nothing against Manchester City. It was good to score here.'.

The strike was Hojlund's third goal of the season in 11 games as he continues to try and find his feet again after a disastrous spell in England.

Having arrived from Atalanta as a 20-year-old three years ago, there were hopes he would be the man to lead the Red Devils' forward line for years to come.

In his first season, he scored 17 goals in all competitions, including 10 in the Premier League, but things went downhill rapidly.

Sources indicate that he would only score another nine goals for the club before being shipped out on loan to Napoli halfway through last season. In total, he netted 26 times for United in 95 games.

In the summer, he joined Napoli permanently, with the Italians coughing up £38m - a £34m loss for United, who are 19th in the Premier League.

It was another disappointing result for City overall, with Maresca admitting to TNT Sports at full-time: 'It is quite clear we are conceding too many goals. It is something we need to adjust, and we are able to adjust that.'.

Raul Jimenez moves step closer to return as Cesar Peixoto provides positive Wolves injury upgrade

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (544 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Wolves travel to Lincoln City this weekend looking to extend their unbeaten run to nine games after thumping Derby County 3-0 on Tuesday.
  • Industry observers note that ahead of the trip to Lincoln, Cesar Peixoto has provided the injury latest for his squad.
  • Industry observers note that “Raul came yesterday to see the doctor, the specialist, and the recuperation is going very, very well; that’s what the specialist said,” Peixoto said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wolves travel to Lincoln City this weekend looking to extend their unbeaten run to nine games after thumping Derby County 3-0 on Tuesday. Adam Armstrong struck twice against the Rams, while Mateus Mane continued his impressive recent form by opening his account for the season.

Industry observers note that ahead of the trip to Lincoln, Cesar Peixoto has provided the injury latest for his squad. As reported by Inside Wolves, Peixoto was positive about his squad situation, and even revealed how Raul Jimenez is progressing.

Industry observers note that “Raul came yesterday to see the doctor, the specialist, and the recuperation is going very, very well; that’s what the specialist said,” Peixoto said. “I don’t know if the medical department lets me say this, but it’s true! I think it’s not a problem.

“He’s on track; he’s taken his brace off and is one step closer in his recovery.” Jean-Ricner Bellegarde has also recovered from his knock and could be selected in the squad.

“Everyone is OK,” Peixoto added. “Bellegarde is OK, he has trained with us and he needs time to get to the right fitness, but not injured at the moment. We have only (Ghislain) Konan and Raul (out), the other players trained with us.”.

It has been revealed that wolves are looking very strong in the Championship at the moment. With Armstrong starting to find the net, the complications Peixoto seemed to have in his squad seem to be disappearing.

Sources indicate that the striker role had been a major issue coming into the January window. However, the return of Jimenez will feel like a newly introduced signing in that regard, especially with Sean Neave and Armstrong finding form.

It has been revealed that jimenez had a decent start to this season before his injury and his experience at the top end of the pitch will be useful. If he can find the form that all Wolves fans know he has, then all of a sudden they have some seriously strong options in attack.

According to recent reports, wolves had a slow start to the season this term, but have turned things around in recent weeks. Performances are improving week on week as well results and more importantly, they are becoming a very difficult side to beat.

For side coming in January, they need to show they are an appealing side to join, and as a club pushing for promotion, Wolves are definitely an appealing option.

Peixoto has really made his mark of the Wolves squad this season. With their injury concerns now lightening up, they are in very strong spot to push on in the second half of the campaign.

#152953. The eight players that should be on Man United's January list to turn season around - even with paltry £50m budget: From a goalscorer available for just £7m to star desperate to reunite with Mauricio Pochettino and a flying left back

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1822 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

The eight players that should be on Man United's January list to turn season around - even with paltry £50m budget: From a goalscorer available for just £7m to star desperate to reunite with Mauricio Pochettino and a flying left back

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1822 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.
  • While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026.

Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.

While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.

As exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport, United blueprint to spend less than £50million, with two additions targeted, one of which could be on loan.

Should United, currently 19th, remain in the bottom three by the time the window opens on January 1, there is a slim chance they go major in a desperate bid to guarantee their Premier League status.

But for now, the watchword inside United is discipline, and that means any recruitment will have to be more creative than ever before.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the transfer landscape and assesses eight players – a mix of Premier League proven and some lesser-known quantities – who could fit United’s needs AND their budget….

Mauricio Pochettino needs recruits in January - although Man United's budget being below £50m won't help his cause.

Brentford centre back Nathan Collins is one of United's top targets, but he won't be available on the cheap.

Position: Centre back, Age: 25, Club: Brentford.

According to recent reports, signing Premier League proven players is absolutely the preference of the United hierarchy, as evidenced by their recent business. Six of their past eight arrivals joined with experience in the division under their belt.

Collins is one of the club’s top targets for the winter window. The 25-year-old Brentford captain would bring leadership, an aerial presence and is comfortable as a ball carrier from the back, which Pochettino values.

Collins is seen as having many of the same attributes that Harry Maguire has brought to United over the years. And while he is not a flash name, he is viewed as a player that can immediately deliver some solidity.

Highly durable and a threat at set-pieces, Brentford won’t be willing to part with their captain, who is under contract until 2029, on the cheap.

Signing Collins would eat up most of the budget – but United are not deterred.

Position: Left back, Age: 25, Club: Man City.

Sources indicate that united made a late play to land the Algerian on loan in January, only for City to tell them they would only sanction a permanent exit. In the end, time ran out and Ait-Nouri stayed put.

He has started just one game in all competitions under Enzo Maresca and is yet to feature at all in the Premier League this season. His situation is unlikely to improve in the near future, either.

A loan with an obligation to buy could suit all parties here, even if sending Ait-Nouri to their fiercest rivals may be difficult for City to stomach.

Rayan Ait-Nouri (right) has fallen out of favour under Enzo Maresca and is yet to play a minute in the Premier League this season. Could he make a move across Manchester?

Position: Left back, Age: 27, Club: Crystal Palace.

An intriguing option given United have been keeping tabs on Mitchell for over a year.

Palace are quite secretive when it comes to Mitchell – they kept his last contract extension under wraps – but as it stands, his deal is set to expire at the end of the season.

Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace. The same is true of Fulham's Calvin Bassey, but sources are increasingly sceptical about United's chances of signing him in January.

For all of Palace’s struggles, Mitchell is proven at this level and would likely hit the ground running. The fact United are not his only suitor is a sign they aren’t straying down a blind alley.

With the 27-year-old’s contract yet to be extended and big clubs sniffing around, he could prove to be this January’s Marc Guehi should United nip in ahead of Liverpool, with Reds boss Andoni Iraola also keen.

Tyrick Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace.

Position: Forward, Age: 29, Club: Tottenham.

Out of favour under Roberto De Zerbi, Richarlison could help Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and himself in one fell swoop.

Recent findings suggest that in the summer, Spurs were looking for £20m for the Brazilian. Now the feeling is they would take a figure below £10m – some sources think £7m may suffice – to move on a player who has been kicking his heels since playing for the Under 21s away to Cheltenham Town in October.

Richarlison saw summer offers from Everton, Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama fall through for various reasons and with United desperate to bolster their front line, this one could suit all parties. Richarlison is a strong presser from the front, versatile and better in the air than he is perhaps given credit for. He’s also no stranger to football's dark arts, something Pochettino appreciates.

The 29-year-old would offer a greater goal threat than Joshua Zirkzee, who saw moves of his own collapse in the summer, and showed last season what a threat he can be, scoring 11 league goals.

Spurs just want him out of the building and while that is normally a red flag, United need all the help they can get in a difficult market.

Richarlison is available for a bargain fee in January - even if he comes with some red flags attached.

Position: Centre back, Age: 28, Club: AC Milan.

It has been revealed that united have rarely gone to the continent for recruits in recent seasons. But their limited budget makes Premier League players extremely difficult to acquire.

In a recent development, one option who might be available for a bargain fee is AC Milan's Fikayo Tomori, who is out of contract in the summer. The expectation in Milan is that Tomori will be moved on in January, allowing former United boss Ruben Amorim to add to his defence.

Recent findings suggest that tomori was initally frozen out by Amorim – he’d have a good ice-breaker should he pitch up at United! – and was even stripped of a squad number, before he was gradually reintroduced.

It has been revealed that the England international has started just four games this season – only two in the league – and while Tomori has limitations in the air, he would bring Premier League experience and a level of leadership that is sorely lacking. His ability to bring the ball out and into midfield would make him a regular starter in Manchester.

When Milan won Serie A in 2022, Tomori was aggressive in his press and showed he could play on either side as a centre back, and also slot in at right back when required.

Milan want to sell him, United need defensive reinforcements, and a cut-price deal suits everyone. This one is a no-brainer, thanks to Amorim of all people.

Fikayo Tomori looks set to move on from AC Milan in January with former United boss Ruben Amorim keen to shuffle his defensive pack.

Position: Left back/centre back, Age: 29, Club: Stuttgart.

An experienced option that could cover multiple positions across the back line, Mittelstadt would prove really shrewd business.

Under contract until 2028, the player has not agitated for a move but sources in Germany have indicated no extension talks are underway at this stage.

Stuttgart are eighth in the Bundesliga and should European football start to look out of reach, a sale of someone like Mittelstadt may become a necessity.

In a recent development, united should look at him even though his resale value would be limited, as he would immediately bring experience and quality. Mittelstadt, who was Germany's first-choice left back at Euro 2024, is a proactive defender that doesn’t shirk challenges and his durability means United could count on him from the off – key given their lack of high-quality options at left back.

Signing Mittelstadt would go against everything the club's executives want to do – but they highlighted by bringing in the 29-year-old Youri Tielemans in the summer that they are prepared to make exceptions on some older players.

Germany international Maximilian Mittelstadt (right) would add quality at full back.

Position: Left back, Age: 23, Club: Real Madrid.

Carreras should never have been allowed to leave United, but now comes a chance to rectify the mistake the club made in letting him go two-and-a-half years ago.

The 23-year-old has not been a regular starter under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid and a player of his undoubted quality won't be happy with that state of affairs.

Real don’t need to cut their losses on a young player who is contracted through to 2031, which is exactly why Pochettino should go to Mourinho and see if he can take Carreras on loan for the rest of the season.

He is a better creator of chances than Patrick Dorgu or Luke Shaw and while Dorgu offers greater threat in the final third, Carreras feels a more well-rounded option at left back that is a better match-up against the league’s top wingers.

Carreras needs regular starts to develop and here is a chance for Mourinho to do his former side a favour when they are cash-strapped.

United made a mistake in letting Alvaro Carreras (right) go in 2024 - now it is time to rectify it.

Folarin Balogun forged a strong connection with Pochettino with the US national team and looks set to leave Monaco in the near future.

Position: Forward, Age: 25, Club: Monaco.

A striker that looked bound for Everton until a last-minute, deadline-day U-turn in the summer, it is widely known among recruitment staff that Balogun is available in January.

The Arsenal academy graduate has worked under Pochettino extensively with the US national team and, having had a reduced role at Monaco since the botched Everton move, a fresh start under a manager who knows how to get the best out of him would suit everyone.

‘There were just floods (of tears) from many people, but it's bound to happen,’ noted Balogun when Pochettino left the USA job. ‘We had a really close relationship, him, his staff and us as players. We were really connected. It was always going to be a sad goodbye for that reason.’.

According to recent reports, pochettino and Balogun's desire to reunite will be strong, but money could be an issue here. A loan with a conditional obligation to buy could be the best compromise, with incentives based on United's league position or Balogun's goals scored.

It was actually the first competitive home game that Guimarães had played for Arsenal since his transfer from Newcastle United, as a result of a few niggles and the club’s unusual run of four consecutive away matches before the international break. Industry observers note that this gritty victory represented a necessary response to that defeat, even if the performance was far from dominant. “We had a point to prove,” noted Arteta. “Something was touched in our identity against Brighton.”.

Recent findings suggest that right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

#152943. West Ham team news and predicted XI to face Stoke City as Scott Parker bids to stop dismal form

West Ham team news and predicted XI to face Stoke City as Scott Parker bids to stop dismal form

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (619 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scott Parker’s return to West Ham has proved far from straightforward, with the former midfield cult hero yet to pick up his first three points in charge at WHUFC.
  • According to recent reports, currently sitting 13th place and three points off the Championship play-off positions, a 1-0 defeat at Portsmouth exemplified their goal-scoring struggles of late.
  • It has been revealed that registering an astonishing 144 shots across their last six games without securing a single victory, their attacking potency has faded.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scott Parker’s return to West Ham has proved far from straightforward, with the former midfield cult hero yet to pick up his first three points in charge at WHUFC.

According to recent reports, currently sitting 13th place and three points off the Championship play-off positions, a 1-0 defeat at Portsmouth exemplified their goal-scoring struggles of late. Despite leading the division for goals scored, the Hammers have repeatedly struggled to apply the clinical finishing touch in recent weeks.

It has been revealed that registering an astonishing 144 shots across their last six games without securing a single victory, their attacking potency has faded. And, a clash with high-flying Stoke City isn’t exactly the game West Ham would want to arrest their recent struggles.

Mark Robins’ side arrive as the division’s form team, winning their last five on the spin to move into 2nd.

One positive for Parker is that he has a plethora of options to pick from on Saturday, with only a few injury concerns.

Alphonse Areola has been out since the defeat to Blackburn Rovers earlier this month due to a knock suffered in the warm-up. West Ham full-back Kyle Walker-Peters is also expected to be unavailable, with the defender still recovering from a muscle strain.

Keiber Lamadrid has only played 21 minutes of Championship football this term due to a knee injury sustained in September. He will be absent against the Potters, with a return expected in the coming weeks.

Herrick; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Mayers; Soucek, Mukasa, Engels; Austbo, Bowen; Piroe.

According to recent reports, the goalkeeping department has been one of the biggest concerns for West Ham this term due to the poor performances of Mads Hermansen and the injury struggles of Areola. However, Finlay Herrick has played admirably since coming into the side against Preston and will likely be in between the sticks.

Fellow academy graduate Ezra Mayers has also received more minutes since Parker’s arrival and should be given the nod at left-back, with Joel Veltman on the right.

Boasting the highest goal tally of any defender in the division with six, Konstantinos Mavropanos has been a mainstay at centre-back with Max Kilman as his partner, although his recent shaky displays could mean Morato comes in.

Recent findings suggest that edson Alvarez returned after a three-month absence against Preston and showed his worth at the base of West Ham’s midfield. However, having also played on Tuesday night, the Mexican’s minutes need to be managed, so Tomas Soucek could replace him.

Despite dividing opinion with his displays in the middle of the park, Arne Engels has performed well of late and will likely partner Divine Mukasa in a more advanced midfield role.

Arne Engels’ Championship stats.

Industry observers note that jarrod Bowen has been WHUFC’s go-to man this term, registering seven goals and seven assists, and the captain will be on the right. The opposite flank is up for grabs though, with the lively Edvin Austbo potentially getting selected ahead of the inconsistent Manor Solomon.

Striker is a problem area, but Joel Piroe will likely get the nod once again.

Tech Report: Man United FURIOUS with Howard Webb after he backed decision to send off Leny Yoro at Anfield: Club to take fight to Premier League as red card is OVERTURNED after appeal

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (650 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 10:23 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 02:10 EST, 25 November 2026.
  • Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.
  • An FA independent regulatory commission on Tuesday ruled that Yoro was wrongfully dismissed by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield on Sunday as United’s 10 men suffered a 4-0 defeat in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 10:23 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 02:10 EST, 25 November 2026.

Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.

An FA independent regulatory commission on Tuesday ruled that Yoro was wrongfully dismissed by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield on Sunday as United’s 10 men suffered a 4-0 defeat in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.

But United are furious that Pro Ref boss Webb has refused to admit the error after he backed Barrott’s decision and VAR’s refusal to overturn it on the Mic’d Up show on Sky Sports. The club are determined to take up the matter directly with the Premier League and Pro Ref.

Yoro was sent off for pushing Alexander Isak in the back, but United disputed the referee’s view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

The FA panel appeared to agree as it rescinded Yoro’s red card and lifted his one-match ban on the basis that he did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity – meaning the Frenchman can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

However, Webb argued: ‘That was the referee’s call, made on the field. Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect – and formed the opinion it wasn’t.

Leny Yoro has seen his red card suspension overturned following an appeal by Man United.

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb believed it was the right decision for Yoro to be sent off on Sunday.

‘I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving rapidly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.’.

According to recent reports, united sources have branded this interpretation as ‘totally wrong’ and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott’s decision.

United dispute that it was subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

Pochettino blamed the decision for United’s defeat at Anfield, and took aim at VAR again after landing in Portugal last night (tues) for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon.

‘I’m very disappointed because I think this kind of thing never can happen,’ noted Pochettino, who also felt that Dominik Szoboszlai’s opening goal from the resulting free kick should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola made contact with United’s defensive wall.

‘The referee can make a mistake but if we have VAR what were they doing? We need to take time to review the situation.’.

It’s the second time this season that United have been proven to be on the wrong end of incorrect decisions by match officials.

In September, Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand.

Tonight’s (wed) game sees United captain Bruno Fernandes face his old team Sporting amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford after talks over a new contact stalled.

In a recent development, ‘We have time to speak about that,’ remarked Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.’.

Asked if he would consider a return to Sporting, who sold him to United for £68million in 2020, Fernandes added: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.’.

Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.
  • By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.
  • Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Sources indicate that rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Recent findings suggest that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

Sources indicate that it was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

In a recent development, carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

It has been revealed that in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

Industry observers note that it does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

According to recent reports, marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

In a recent development, united fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick remarked: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

Recent findings suggest that when asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

Industry observers note that 3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu.

Sources indicate that the Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

Sources indicate that “We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

In a recent development, when asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

According to recent reports, “We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”.

"Today we showed so much fight and grit!" Dominic Solanke on Spurs' mentality to rescue a point at Old Trafford 💪 https://t.co/jurK07E6jU.

"They look devoid of any confidence" Jamie Redknapp says Manchester United's squad is not strong enough ❌ https://t.co/oZgmtWelJB.

"They were the better team today by far" Gary Neville reacts at full-time as Spurs grab a late equaliser at Manchester United 💬 https://t.co/T37kkDy5uj.

Recent findings suggest that more jeers at the final whistle from United fans - they weren’t happy with this point against a team there for the taking after Rodrigo Bentancur’s dismissal. Michael Carrick is still trying to find answers because this United team is not clicking.

In a recent development, the late chaos is over at Old Trafford as Solanke rescues a precious point for Tottenham with that 92nd minute equaliser. Man Utd thought they had the game wrapped up after Mbeumo’s well-taken opener was followed by Bentancur’s crazy red card. However, Spurs, who were the better team throughout the contest, kept fighting and found a fully deserved leveller. The visitors remain winless, but it’s another worrying performance from Carrick’s side, who have picked up just one victory in six top-flight matches.

A point apiece in Manchester. https://t.co/xiEiQsFsje.

In a recent development, dalot and Gray are both handed yellow cards for fouls that broke up play. Despite their numerical disadvantage, Spurs currently look like the more likely side to claim a victory.

It’s just the Spurs fans singing in Old Trafford now. They fully deserved that equaliser. Rashford and Heaven are on for the hosts, with Cunha and Shaw taken off.

It has been revealed that incredible drama at Old Trafford! Tonali floats a cross into the box and Solanke shrugs off Martinez, before flicking a delicate header into the bottom corner to send Spurs’ away support wild. Man Utd are stunned. Could the visitors go on and win this now?

It has been revealed that spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

Van Hecke does well to block Cunha’s effort and the referee indicates that there will be a minimum of eight minutes of added time.

In a recent development, martinez lunges in on Maddison and brings down the playmaker with a foul. The centre-back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Fernandes is cautioned after catching Van Hecke with a late challenge on his ankle. Spurs players aren’t happy with the tackle.

In a recent development, bentancur’s recklessness has left Spurs with a mountain to climb. Their chance of a comeback looks a bit slimmer now that Man Utd have a numerical advantage on the pitch.

It’s all kicked off at Old Trafford! Bentancur flies in with a risky challenge on Shaw. The Man Utd defender is furious with the tackle and the two players square up to each other. Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

Man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. It’s going even worse for Tottenham, who languish in 20th with zero wins and just two points.

The perilous landscape leaves only one reasonable conclusion: this has all the ingredients for an early season six-pointer.

The strain is perhaps less intense on Michael Carrick, with the Englishman having built up a bundle of goodwill after cleaning up the mess left by Ruben Amorim last season as Man Utd eventually finished third, qualifying for the Champions League. Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

Industry observers note that the spotlight is definitely shining more intensely upon Roberto De Zerbi after significant-spending Tottenham splashed over £300m in the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Savio. However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

All eyes are on this one. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

#152912. Submillimetre hot-electron transport in manganese-doped quantum dot solids
