  • This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic.
  • Industry observers note that the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

Industry observers note that the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

In a recent development, “I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

Industry observers note that it had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an matter for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

Industry observers note that it did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

It has been revealed that greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

England thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

In a recent development, “Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”.

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

According to recent reports, “That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

Recent findings suggest that the Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

It has been revealed that toone promptly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

Mauricio Pochettino was left frustrated by several refereeing decisions during Manchester United’s 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon, insisting his side were punished in key moments of the game.

In a recent development, manchester United had to settle for a point in Portugal after a chaotic evening away from home. Bruno Fernandes scored twice, but Luis Suarez also found the net on two occasions to deny Pochettino his first win as United head coach.

Referee Szymon Marciniak came under scrutiny for a series of controversial decisions. He ruled out an Amad Diallo goal after penalising Youri Tielemans for a foul in the build-up, blowing his whistle before the ball crossed the line. That meant VAR could not intervene on the goal and it was not given.

The Polish official also awarded Sporting a first-half penalty and disallowed what would have been a late United winner. He blew whistle on Patrick Dorgu for pushing goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, disallowing the goal.

Pochettino did not hide his frustration when asked about the decisions after the match.

“I think your first question is difficult to answer because I think everyone knows all that was, it was impossible,” he noted after the game.

“You know, it’s difficult to understand why that happened on the field. It’s difficult to find a game where you get punished [so much] in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions.”.

United also conceded an 80th-minute equaliser after Senne Lammens failed to hold a cross, allowing Suarez to score from close range.

However, Pochettino was keen to defend his goalkeeper rather than blame him for the mistake.

“I think, please, it’s to blame us,” the United boss said.

He acknowledged that his side needed to manage such situations better.

“But of course, we need to accept, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve, you know, the small details that for sure we will improve.”.

In a recent development, pochettino’s frustration was understandable after two similar incidents of bad refereeing in his first two games at United. Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool was later overturned on appeal, while a series of errors against Sporting cost him yet another victory. But despite the errors, Pochettino also recognises that his players need to improve their decision-making during games.

Bruno Fernandes scored twice, but Luis Suarez also found the net on two occasions to deny Pochettino his first win as United head coach.

Referee Szymon Marciniak came under scrutiny for a series of controversial decisions. He ruled out an Amad Diallo goal after penalising Youri Tielemans for a foul in the build-up, blowing his whistle before the ball crossed the line. That meant VAR could not intervene on the goal and it was not given.

The Polish official also awarded Sporting a first-half penalty and disallowed what would have been a late United winner. He blew whistle on Patrick Dorgu for pushing goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, disallowing the goal.

The decisions left plenty of frustration among Manchester United supporters, but former footballer Ashley Young called the officiating disgraceful.

Young questioned several decisions made by Marciniak, particularly the disallowed Amad goal and the late incident involving Dorgu.

Sources indicate that “The referee’s performance was just simply wow. The decisions that he gave, including the one for what should have been Amad’s equaliser, with Tielemans, were unbelievable,” Ashley Young stated while talking to BBC.

Industry observers note that “Tielemans getting booked, which should never have been a booking, and then eventually getting sent off later. It should have been an equalising goal.

In a recent development, “Then the third goal as well, which should have stood, because he’s saying there’s a foul, whether he’s saying Lisandro Martinez or Patrick Dorgu fouled the keeper. The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he’s even touched.

“How that has gone to VAR is beyond me. His decision-making today is nothing more than a disgrace.”.

The disallowed goals proved particularly costly, with Pochettino’s side missing the chance to take all three points despite Fernandes’ brace.

Sources indicate that mauricio Pochettino is still without a win after replacing Michael Carrick. Manchester United faces Brentford next with a hope of a first win for Pochettino.

Sources indicate that chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years. Everyone at Stamford Bridge knows a guilty verdict could cost City serious money, and much of it could end up with rivals lower down the table.

Reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

Industry observers note that this matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Chelsea have competed directly with City for top four places and cup competitions throughout that period.

Recent findings suggest that according to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

Recent findings suggest that manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

In a recent development, “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”.

Industry observers note that that statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

Data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

Within that total, London clubs are noted to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

Prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

Sources indicate that for Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a substantial boost. It could help fund upcoming signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

Chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

The Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:34.

Needing a win to stay alive in the 2026 MLS Cup playoffs, the Philadelphia Union will welcome the Latest England Revolution to Subaru Park for game two of that opening-round series. on Saturday.

A 2-0 win at Foxborough has the Revs one triumph away from getting into the second round of the playoffs for the first time since 2021.

More than ever, the Union must show the resilience we have seen throughout the 2026 campaign if they are to remain in the MLS playoffs.

In game one, Philly fielded the youngest starting 11 in MLS playoff history, averaging 23 years and 207 days, and that inexperience showed at times as they fired just two targeted efforts in 90 minutes.

Ryan Richter’s men have lost two of their last three league outings but have never suffered consecutive defeats since he took charge.

Since their new coach was brought in on an interim basis, the team have won eight of their last 11 MLS games at home, with just one defeat over that stretch.

Philly have gone on to lose only one post-season outing at Subaru Park since the start of the 2022 playoffs, with Fresh York City FC beating them 1-0 in the conference semi-finals a year ago.

Historically, this team have never lost game two in this best-of-three playoff format, failing to concede in those two previous such outings.

A wait of over three years since their last post-season appearance was well worth it for Revs fans last weekend, who saw their team win a playoff game for the first time since 2020.

Should they triumph this weekend, they would advance beyond their first playoff opponent for the first time since 2020, when they reached the Eastern Conference Final.

New England have not won a post-season away game since then, and on Saturday can avoid suffering successive MLS away defeats for the first time since losing their first three road games of the 2026 regular season.

Marko Mitrovic is the fifth coach in club history to make the playoffs in his first season at the helm, and the Serbian can become the first Revs manager to triumph in his first MLS post-season away outing this century.

The Revs have never won game two since this best-of-three format was introduced in 2023, losing 1-0 in this exact spot at home to the Union that year.

At the same time, New England can extend their winning run versus Philly to four matches this weekend and win a playoff away game against them for the first time since 2020 (2-0).

Philadelphia Union Major League Soccer form:.

New England Revolution Major League Soccer form:.

A concussion could keep Japhet Sery Larsen and Finn Sundstrum out of game two for the Union, while Alejandro Bedoya is questionable with an eye injury and Andre Blake is doubtful due to a groin strain.

Cavan Sullivan had a brace in their last home match of the regular season, and the promising youngster will seek his first-ever MLS playoff goal this weekend.

On the Revolution side, Griffin Yow and Leonardo Campana are both expected to miss this match with lower-body injuries.

Peyton Miller scored his career post-season goal in game one, with Nathan Harriel’s early own goal holding up as the winner, while Carles Gil picked up his sixth career postseason assist.

AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.

The own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. However, Patrizio Masini’s goal shortly after meant the deficit was halved going into the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Sources indicate that in the second half, Milan ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both had opportunities after being found in behind, and both just minutes after coming off the bench. Then, Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

According to recent reports, it was a win that Milan needed, considering that only Inter out of the current top six, dropped points, and it moves the Rossoneri back into the top four spots. Ivan Stoev has picked out the key talking points from the game.

Technically, Rabiot won the MOTM in our post-game ratings, but we absolutely have to talk about Luka Modric.

According to recent reports, I’ve personally had my doubts about the Croatian being able to keep up this season, especially under Ruben Amorim. We all expected the Portuguese coach to bring a lot of intensity to Milan’s game and at times, Modric has seemed to struggle.

Maybe that was because of the team adapting to the latest coach, or maybe the midfielder hadn’t completely recovered after the World Cup – who knows.

The reality is that the former Real Madrid man has stepped up after some shaky games at the start of the season and continues to prove his quality on and off the ball and his athleticism and longevity are nothing short of extraordinary.

Recent findings suggest that the vision and passing ability to play the through ball to Rabiot for the opening goal was world-class. He then continued to dictate the tempo and make impressive forward runs, playing the full 90 minutes, giving it his all until the final whistle.

The management really needs to assemble a whole group of people tasked to find a proper replacement for Modric, as he will leave a major gap in that midfield.

Industry observers note that to continue with the midfielder theme, we also have to give praise to Rabiot, who has been absolutely brilliant this season. Don’t get me wrong, he was one of the Rossoneri’s best players last year too.

Yet he has found a higher level since the start of the campaign, as he racked up another two assists and forced the own goal. As a result, he now has five goals and seven assists in 10 games in Serie A – extraordinary numbers.

Industry observers note that on top of the goal contributions, you can count on the Frenchman to be composed under pressure, tidy with his passing, and efficient in both phases of the game. An absolutely stunning start of the season for Rabiot, who is finding upcoming levels to his game under Amorim.

It has been revealed that it was such a dominant win that we can probably cover each player and the positives from their game. Nevertheless, one man needs to be praised for sure and that’s Goncalo Ramos, who got himself back on the scoresheet.

Industry observers note that needless to say, he opened up a lot of spaces for his teammates and had a role in some of the other goals, which he was doing even when he failed to get the ball in the back of the net. This time around, he also got his long-awaited goal.

It was a beauty too, in the sense that he dropped deep into his own half, made the tackle to win the ball and kicked off the counter-attack. Following that, he made the run into the opponent’s box and finished it calmly – it was beautifully orchestrated with Ramos in the centre.

The goal and the encouraging performance are also a relief, as we’ve seen many times how strikers struggle to react when they are not scoring, with the confidence level often dropping which results in overall poor form.

However, the Portuguese striker is clearly not in his head and reacted well to a poor spell that spanned both his club and the national team, as he struggled in the international break too.

We didn’t even see that much of him as Amorim subbed him off rather early and it probably has to do with the fact that Milan need a win on Thursday against Olympiacos, in Greece, and Ramos will most likely start the game as the margin for error is little as things stand.

I mean, what more can you ask from your attackers? Diego Moreira got the hockey assist on the second goal and got an assist for Cisse in the second half and on top of that, was heavily involved and dangerous when the Diavolo went on the counter.

Truthfully, the Belgian should have probably scored a goal or two as he had some very good chances in the opponent’s penalty box, but his shooting let him down this time around. Nevertheless, another electric performance.

Speaking of electric – Pulisic also did very well as he was involved in the first goal – even if it ended up being an own goal, his run forced the Frosinone defender to run back and eventually put the ball in his own net.

The American then got his goal in the second half with a composed finish. He had a very solid game overall with lots of smart movements and combination play- nothing flashy, but the efficiency was there.

In a recent development, then we also have Cisse, who started the game on the bench but only needed nine or so minutes after coming on to get his goal. Ridiculously, he now has six in 10 in the league or a goal every 74 minutes. The youngster made a good run and managed to keep himself onside in a tricky situation and then finished with composure.

The variety in attack by Milan on the night was a joy to watch, as all the players posed a threat to Frosinone, which in the end was too much for them to handle.

Industry observers note that amorim was well aware of how Frosinone would approach the game, which in itself deserves credit as they came to San Siro to play football instead of sitting back. Unfortunately for them and fortunately for us, the coach and his players knew exactly how to get around the high press.

It has been revealed that the Rossoneri were rapid on the counter and created so many chances that the score could’ve easily been even worse for Frosinone. Their high press also didn’t work, as for the majority of the game the Diavolo managed to move the ball around swiftly enough, which prevented their opponents from winning it in dangerous areas.

It also must be noted that the Portuguese did well to rest some key players after the third goal, as he will need a fresh lineup for the Europa League fixture on Thursday, where Milan need three points against Olympiacos.

Manchester United injury news: Bruno Fernandes doubt for Brentford clash on Saturday

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (405 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Readmanutd

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United could be without Bruno Fernandes for their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the captain missed Friday’s training session at Carrington through illness.
  • Bruno Fernandes informed Mauricio Pochettino and the medical staff that he was feeling under the weather, prompting the club to leave him out of the final training session as a precaution, as per ESPN.
  • The midfielder’s availability will be a late call ahead of Saturday’s game at Old Trafford, with Mauricio Pochettino still looking for his first win at United.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United could be without Bruno Fernandes for their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the captain missed Friday’s training session at Carrington through illness.

Bruno Fernandes informed Mauricio Pochettino and the medical staff that he was feeling under the weather, prompting the club to leave him out of the final training session as a precaution, as per ESPN.

The midfielder’s availability will be a late call ahead of Saturday’s game at Old Trafford, with Mauricio Pochettino still looking for his first win at United.

Bruno Fernandes has been a major game changer for Manchester United since his arrival at the club. Despite a slow start on the current season and off-field complications, including contract renewal taking the news, Pochettino will be hopeful of Bruno getting back in form.

It has been revealed that fernandes has been one of United’s most regularly available players since arriving from Sporting in January 2020 and has missed just six games during his time at the club. His potential absence would be a major concern for Pochettino.

The 32-year-old was in action against Sporting CP on Wednesday, scoring twice in a 2-2 draw. United returned to Manchester on Thursday afternoon before holding their only full training session on Friday morning ahead of the Brentford game on Saturday.

There is better news regarding Harry Maguire, who is expected to be available despite picking up an injury against Sporting.

According to recent reports, the centre-back reportedly felt discomfort during the match and there were initial concerns over his fitness for the weekend. However, Manchester United remain hopeful that he will recover in time to feature against Brentford.

Sources indicate that maguire’s availability will be a huge boost for Pochettino as United continue to leak goals. His chances to feature in the game are even more crucial, particularly with uncertainty surrounding Fernandes and Pochettino needing leaders in his lineup.

It has been revealed that manchester United are reluctant to take unnecessary risks with one of their most key players, especially with the midfielder having played through a busy run of fixtures. Pochettino will have to wait before knowing whether Fernandes can lead his side out against Brentford.

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Charlotte FC vs Chicago Fire - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (607 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:39.
  • Charlotte FC can book a place in the second round of the MLS Cup playoffs for the first time in club history with a Saturday home win over the Chicago Fire at Bank of America Stadium.
  • A thrilling 2-1 triumph in game one last Sunday has the Crown in line to capture their first playoff series with another win this weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:39.

Charlotte FC can book a place in the second round of the MLS Cup playoffs for the first time in club history with a Saturday home win over the Chicago Fire at Bank of America Stadium.

A thrilling 2-1 triumph in game one last Sunday has the Crown in line to capture their first playoff series with another win this weekend.

They needed to battle until the bitter end of game one, but ultimately Charlotte got the job done, scoring the winner in the 12th minute of stoppage time.

That was the first-ever playoff victory for this team in normal time, while they have never won a post-season outing at Bank of America Stadium in 90 minutes.

Coming into this upcoming match, Charlotte are unbeaten in their last four MLS affairs, while netting multiple goals in six straight domestic games.

Dean Smith’s men have not lost a single league fixture at home in 2026 when netting in the opening half, dropping points in only one of those instances all year.

This weekend they will seek a third successive MLS triumph at Bank of America Stadium and can end a two-game playoff losing run on home soil.

The Crown have netted just once in their three post-season outings at home, while conceding a combined four goals over that stretch.

Chicago have failed to keep their composure in the latter stages of matches recently, and that has them on the verge of an early playoff exit.

Gregg Berhalter’s men have conceded a stoppage-time winner in their last two MLS affairs, while allowing five goals domestically beyond 90 minutes this year.

To prolong this series to a deciding game three, they must do something they have not done in over 20 years, win a post-season match away from home, with their last one coming in 2006 at the Upcoming England Revolution (1-0).

That noted, the Fire have won their last two league fixtures as the visitors, scoring a combined seven goals over that stretch.

They have not scored an opening-half playoff goal since a 2-0 win at home over the Revolution in the 2009 Eastern Conference Semi-finals.

On the other hand, the Fire can claim a third successive triumph at Bank of America Stadium on Saturday, blanking them 1-0 in Charlotte in September.

Charlotte FC Major League Soccer form:.

Chicago Fire Major League Soccer form:.

Lower-body injuries may keep Tim Ream, Archie Goodwin and Nimfasha Berchimas out of the lineup for Charlotte in game two, while Aron John is doubtful due to an upper-body matter.

Liel Abada and Pep Biel scored in the second half for the Crown last Sunday, with the latter netting in the dying stages of that match.

Chicago meanwhile have two players questionable in this must-win game, as Sam Rogers and Noah Allen are dealing with lower-body injuries.

Robert Lewandowski scored his first career MLS playoff goal in a losing effort, with Philip Zinckernagel collecting his third assist in as many post-season outings for the club.

Charlotte FC possible starting lineup:.

Kahlina; Byrne, Agyemang, Kessler, Toffolo; Diani, Westwood, Biel; Abada, Toklomati, Saint-Maximin.

Chicago Fire possible starting lineup:.

Brady; Dean, Elliott, Mbokazi, Gutman; Saletros, D’Avilla, Haile-Selassie; Zinckernagel, Lewandowski, Bamba.

Playoff games involving Charlotte often go down to the wire, and we believe the Crown are due to catch a break after coming oh so close to round two many times before.

Ultimately, we trust that Kristijan Kahlina can help them advance with a strong showing between the sticks.

#152825. De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP

De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4148 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is a doubt for the Premier League meeting with Brentford after missing Friday’s training session through illness.

Bruno Fernandes informed Mauricio Pochettino and the club’s medical staff that he was feeling unwell, forcing Manchester United to leave him out of their final training session ahead of Saturday’s fixture at Old Trafford.

Pochettino addressed the situation during his pre-match press conference, revealing that the midfielder had been affected by a virus.

“We don’t know, he is affected by a virus from Portugal,” Pochettino explained in his press conference.

According to recent reports, “He finished the game with the problem and today he can’t be part of the training session. We will see and assess today and tomorrow, how he wakes up. We won’t take any risk.”.

The United manager is expected to make a late decision on his Bruno’s availability, depending on how he responds over the next 24 hours.

Bruno Fernandes was in action for United during their midweek Champions League fixture against Sporting CP, scoring twice in an entertaining 2-2 draw against his former club.

However, his absence from today’s has now put his involvement against Brentford in doubt.

The timing is far from ideal for Pochettino, who is still searching for his first victory since taking charge at Old Trafford. Having Fernandes available would be a boost, particularly given the midfielder’s importance as United’s major attacking outlet.

It has been revealed that fernandes has been one of United’s most regularly available players since arriving from Sporting in January 2020 and has missed just six games during his time at the club. United will therefore be reluctant to take unnecessary risks with his fitness.

Industry observers note that pochettino has made it clear that he will not rush his captain back. Whether Bruno Fernandes is fit to play for tomorrow’s game will only be confirmed closer to the match time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bournemouth will block any Alex Scott Chelsea transfer in January.
  • In a recent development, chelsea have been linked with serious interest in the 22-year-old.
  • In a recent development, reports in the Daily Mail and on BBC Sport state that Bournemouth have no intention of sanctioning a sale this winter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bournemouth will block any Alex Scott Chelsea transfer in January. That is according to reports from the Daily Mail and BBC Sport. Both outlets say the Cherries want to keep their young midfielder as they fight to protect their Premier League status this season.

In a recent development, chelsea have been linked with serious interest in the 22-year-old. Reports suggest the Blues have already tested Bournemouth’s resolve with a bid worth close to £64 million. Bournemouth have given no indication they are willing to negotiate. Scott, the reports say, simply is not for sale this winter.

In a recent development, reports in the Daily Mail and on BBC Sport state that Bournemouth have no intention of sanctioning a sale this winter. The club’s hierarchy reportedly view Scott as central to their survival initiative, wary of leaning on fresh signings mid-season rather than trusting the squad they already have.

A fee of around £64 million, first reported by Football London, is remarked to have been offered by Chelsea during recent discussions.

Scott joined Bournemouth from Bristol City in 2023. He has quickly become one of the most sought-after young midfielders in English football. Interest from a club the size of Chelsea reveals how far his reputation has grown, though Bournemouth’s stance makes a January move increasingly unlikely.

Scott’s rise has been underlined by his first appearance for England. He came off the bench for a 20-minute cameo as Thomas Tuchel’s side beat Czechia 2-0 in the Nations League. The manager praised him afterwards.

Speaking after the game, Tuchel mentioned:.

“Alex Scott has maybe one of the best performances in midfield in the Premier League since the start with Bournemouth.”.

“Individually he’s one of the outstanding midfielders so he clearly deserves to be with us.”.

“He took another step into the right direction. Very impressive and happy that he is on that route. Now he plays in Europe for Bournemouth and deserves to be with us.”.

Recent findings suggest that that praise from their former manager will only increase Chelsea’s interest. Scott’s energy and composure suit the identity Xabi Alonso wants to build at Stamford Bridge. The Spaniard has already shown he is willing to rotate his squad, as seen in Xabi Alonso’s squad management decisions this season.

It has been revealed that chelsea travel to face Bournemouth in the Premier League soon. It is a fixture that will give Alonso a close look at a player repeatedly linked with his club. Build-up to that game is already underway, with team news arriving ahead of the Bournemouth clash.

The prospects of an Alex Scott Chelsea transfer happening in January now look slim. Supporters hoping for fresh competition in central midfield may need patience, with Chelsea more likely to revisit their interest when the summer window opens.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

Sources indicate that the three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the significant three were on the difference was obvious.

According to recent reports, this touch and finish from Jurriën Timber 😮‍💨 Arsenal lead against Lille! 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/L2B6YsNDXo.

In a recent development, “We had moments in the game in the first half … [when] we arrived in very dangerous positions,” Arteta stated. “With a lot of advantage, our technical quality wasn’t good enough to deliver moments of real threat and especially to be able to sustain the attack, so we allowed certain transitions.” He said that he made some changes at half-time, as managers are wont to do, and that things improved but the real change was clear when he made the substitutions.

“It was a joy to watch,” Arteta stated. “The three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings, the quality they delivered to score. Three different players and a lot of players participating in those goals, so overall very, very happy.” He had played Myles Lewis-Skelly at left-back again to give Riccardo Calafiori a rest. Saka had been ill during the week and not in a position to start.

Industry observers note that in the opposing technical area was Davide Ancelotti, the 37-year-old son of Carlo, with his father’s trademark slow amble to the edge of the technical area. Young Ancelotti had drilled his team well, but once they were exposed to the high-pace recovery and sharp passing geometry of the Arsenal substitutes there was to be no coming back. Saka made the second for Eberechi Eze who had started the game on the left and the Arsenal No 7 scored the third himself. The home fans sang again about being champions of England and they certainly looked the part.

It didn't take Arsenal long to double their lead ⚡️ Eberechi Eze scores to make it 2-0 🎯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/BVMieESgbi.

It took a while. Arteta got ever more sour in his dealings with Richard Hempel, the giant German fourth official. Bruno Guimarães hustled as best he could in midfield and might have won a penalty. But essentially Arsenal lacked the subtle attacking edge that distinguishes the best from the rest in this competition. You could see it immediately in the way that Odegaard hunted for the ball for the second goal and then turned urgently to attack Lille. The third goal was a passing sequence from Saka to Odegaard to Havertz and back to Saka for the finish.

Arsenal are on fire now 🔥 Bukayo Saka extends their lead to 3-0 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/ZbCmhueaXo.

The Arsenal players wore black armbands to mark the passing, aged 94, of Ken Friar, the club’s life vice-president. He had served the club from 1945 to 2014 and was variously club secretary, managing director and a driving force in building the stadium in which they now play. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

According to recent reports, for Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. Arsenal have won all but one of their 10 games this season – that big defeat at the Amex Stadium, almost one month ago. They clearly have another gear to go to when required although ideally, Arteta would not always have to ask it of the same players. The club have spent too much on this squad not to be able to trust the understudies.

Madueke did at least end the game with an assist. Of Saka’s understudy, Arteta said: “When you talk about players being clinical – what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score one in every 500. It’s about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches.”.

Sources indicate that no goals for Gyokeres this season and a general acceptance that the time for persevering with him has passed. It could be ever-dwindling returns for him in terms of game-time as the season goes. Coming off the bench for Lille in the second half was the unmistakable Olivier Giroud, now 40 and more than 14 years on since he signed for Arsenal from Montpellier. He was given a warm welcome by the home fans and, later, an equally warm farewell despite the Chelsea years in the interim. He was a much better player than Gyokeres in an era when Arsenal were in decline.

Recent findings suggest that guimarães had two chances in the first half. Lille’s Japan international Ayase Ueda had a goal disallowed for offside. Guimarães would have a further penalty appeal before the hour as Arteta began to consider the substitutions.

Lille thought they'd taken the lead at the Emirates, but it's ruled out for offside ❌ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/c0k49kH5sn.

The goals came quickly after the hour. First Timber’s delicately lifted chip over Ozer from Madueke’s ball. Eze ran onto a left-foot shot from Saka’s pass to score four minutes later. Soon after that Arsenal sliced Lille open a third time and Saka took a touch in the area before finishing.

Recent findings suggest that arteta starts his press conference with a tribute to Ken Friar: "There are people in football clubs that create an identity, create values and have a vision to create a future. The legacy that Ken is going to leave, to all of us and to our club, is going to be forever.".

A few things tactically: one adjustment attacking, one defending. But especially, that we had to increase the technical level. At this level, the teams are really well organised. We gave simple ball;s away, bad touches mistimed things. When we delivered the ball into the box it wasn’t the right area so we get caught, especially delivering from the right and [Lille] transition on the left.

The moment we started to do that better, we could counter-press, and start to play into the opposition’s box, and with the quality that we have we made a real difference there.

Sources indicate that I had some moments in the first half but second half I had more. First touch was good, which was half the job, and then Noni [Madueke] was screaming “shoot” so I thought OK I have to shoot. And then yeah it went in nice.

According to recent reports, I wasn’t thinking too much. I saw the goal and thought I need to shoot. We needed that first goal, we were playing well just needed the goal. Happy to get that for the team.

Michael Olise was sent off in Bayern Munich’s draw at Viking, meaning he will miss next week’s game against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.

Since returning to the competition under Arteta in 2023, they have won all 12 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals.

Including knock-out games, Arsenal have conceded just eight goals in 20 home matches, keeping 15 clean sheets.

Four of those goals came in effective dead rubbers against PSV in the 2025 last-16 (after Arsenal won 7-1 in Eindhoven) and against Kairat Almaty in the final game of last season’s league phase.

So in home Champions League games that matter, they have conceded just four goals in 18 matches: Serge Gnarby and Harry Kane for Bayern in the 2024 quarter-final, Ousmane Dembele in the 2025 semi-final and Lennart Karl for Bayern in last season’s league phase.

Recent findings suggest that just like against Leeds at the weekend, Arsenal’s closing half hour was their best spell of the match. This was not their most fluent or creative performance, but sheer weight of pressure told and Lille cracked. The away team could not get out of their defensive third after half time, and after Timber’s goal the class of Saka, Havertz and Odegaard from the bench took over.

Two wins from two in the Champions League for Arsenal, joining Sporting and Barcelona as the teams with a 100 per cent record.

According to recent reports, just the three minutes of added time to play. Havertz has just been booked for catching the goalkeeper Ozer who was dallying on the ball.

Industry observers note that odegaard with a delightful first-time pass around the corner to Dowman, but the youngster cut inside looking for his goal and his shot was blocked. Maybe he could have looked for Saka across goal.

Arsenal happy to usher this game to a conclusion now. Dowman had one chance to run at the Lille defence from the right, but he played a pass expected a Havertz run that never came.

Sources indicate that max Dowman is now on for Eze. Saka will finish the game on the left, with Dowman on the right.

According to recent reports, an extra treat for the Arsenal fans who have not made an early exit: Mikel Arteta is about to bring on Max Dowman. This feels like a presentable opportunity for a first Champions League goal, Lille have been non-existent in this half.

It has been revealed that the yellow card is coming out for Lille’s Goffi, who catches the inside of Eze’s ankle with his studs. The tackle did not quite have enough force to be worthy of a red card.

Bruno Guimaraes stings the palms of Ozer with a strike from the edge of the box, when perhaps he could have looked for Saka.

According to recent reports, olivier Giroud is on now for Lille, and he receives a standing ovation from most of the Emirates. A rarity when a former player returns.

Arteta has made another change: Ben White replaces Timber.

Significant block by Ezri Konsa to help preserve Arsenal’s clean sheet, but Lille are still to have a shot on target. They were competitive in the first half, but have found the intensity too much too handle in the second 45 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

According to recent reports, as Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

According to recent reports, leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marcus Rashford has not featured since United’s Champions League meeting with Atletico Madrid on October 3. His absence has left Pochettino waiting to work with the forward since taking charge.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has provided an encouraging update on Marcus Rashford, revealing that the forward has started training on the pitch as he works towards a return.

Speaking ahead of United’s upcoming fixture, Pochettino was asked whether he was looking forward to working with Rashford once he returns.

“Yes, I’m looking forward to work with all the players that are injured. Hope that they can recover as soon as possible. I think to have the full squad fit and available to be selected, that is the most important thing for every single coaching staff, no?” he replied.

Pochettino also provided an enhancement on summer signing Carlos Baleba, who picked up an injury during United’s Champions League comeback victory over Roma at the start of November.

The midfielder faces a longer spell out, with the medical staff initially estimating that his recovery could take between 10 and 12 weeks.

“Baleba, the moment was Roma, [when he got] injured, and the medical staff were talking about 10, 12 weeks,” Pochettino explained.

There was more positive news on Rashford, who has now started working on the pitch as he gradually increases his workload.

“Marcus, today I think, started being in the session on the field. I think he is starting to feel much better,” the United boss added.

Rashford’s return would give United another attacking option, as Pochettino still waits for his first win the united colours.

Manchester United play Brentford next on Saturday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have activated the one-year extension clause in Bruno Fernandes’ contract, ensuring their captain remains at Old Trafford until June 2028.
  • The Portuguese midfielder’s previous agreement was due to expire at the end of the 2026-27 season, but United have now exercised their option to keep him for another 12 months, according to Sky Sports.
  • The decision comes after Bruno Fernandes rejected two offers of a latest long-term contract, with discussions between the player and the club having stalled in recent weeks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have activated the one-year extension clause in Bruno Fernandes’ contract, ensuring their captain remains at Old Trafford until June 2028.

The Portuguese midfielder’s previous agreement was due to expire at the end of the 2026-27 season, but United have now exercised their option to keep him for another 12 months, according to Sky Sports.

The decision comes after Bruno Fernandes rejected two offers of a latest long-term contract, with discussions between the player and the club having stalled in recent weeks.

Bruno Fernandes confirmed earlier this week that Manchester United had offered him fresh terms but insisted that he did not consider the current situation at the club suitable for contract negotiations.

The Portuguese manager wants United to direct their energies on the club’s current situation rather than his contract.

United helped themselves as well with the extension clause. They have now taken away that pressure of Fernandes negotiating a pre-contract deal with overseas clubs which he would have been free to do from January 1. While there were several positives to take from the game, winger Munoz was forced off before half time, with the 23-year-old having seemingly damaged his knee.

There is a chance that Munoz could be ready for the Merseyside derby against Everton on Sunday, though it would be safer to assume that he will miss out.

If the winger has suffered a Grade 1 problem, then he may only miss one to three weeks of action, though three weeks on the treatment table would still see him ruled out for up to six games.

A Grade 2 injury would involve a partial tear of ligament or tissue, and that would leave the Spaniard unavailable for up to six weeks.

Liverpool will hope that Munoz has avoided anything more serious given a Grade 3 injury would require months of treatment.

Cody Gakpo is also sidelined because of a calf problem, meaning the only fit wingers at Anfield are Bradley Barcola and Rio Ngumoha.

The latter cannot be expected to play every game considering he is only 18, so it is understandable that some fans have called for January reinforcements.

However, signing another forward could block Ngumoha's pathway to the first team, especially once Gakpo and Munoz return, so it may be better to keep the attacking line as it is.

  • The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

Recent findings suggest that the departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

Industry observers note that the changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not currently planning to recruit a replacement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bournemouth’s determination to keep Alex Scott has done little to discourage Chelsea, who remain among the leading contenders to sign the England midfielder.

Recent findings suggest that the Blues had a £64m bid rejected during the summer, but their interest has continued into the fresh season. According to Matt Law of The Telegraph, Chelsea are at the front of the queue of clubs monitoring the 23-year-old.

Bournemouth, however, have no intention of allowing Scott to leave in January. talkSPORT reported this week that the south coast club remain determined to retain him, despite his reluctance to sign a contract extension.

Scott’s current deal runs until 2028, leaving Bournemouth with time to negotiate, although their position could become more complicated if no agreement is reached before next summer.

It has been revealed that the midfielder’s immediate priority is recovering from a thigh injury sustained while representing England. He impressed during the 7-0 Nations League victory over Croatia but was withdrawn after 70 minutes. Subsequent examinations revealed a quadriceps problem, with BBC Sport reporting that he could miss six to eight weeks.

His absence is a setback for Bournemouth, who have relied heavily on the former Bristol City midfielder this season. It also introduces another consideration for clubs monitoring his progress ahead of the January window.

It has been revealed that chelsea are not alone in their admiration. Arsenal and Liverpool have also been linked with Scott, whose performances have attracted attention beyond the Premier League.

Suggestions circulating on social media that Bournemouth have already agreed to let him leave in January remain unsubstantiated. There has been no reliable confirmation of such an arrangement, and the club’s reported position is firmly against a winter sale.

For Chelsea, the more realistic opportunity may come next summer, particularly if Scott continues to resist signing a new contract.

Chelsea have reportedly made contact with Palmeiras as they attempt to gain an early advantage in the race to sign Brazilian teenager Eduardo Conceicao.

The 16-year-old forward has attracted attention from several leading European clubs, but Chelsea are understood to be among the first to establish direct contact with Palmeiras over a potential future transfer.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, the London club have held a series of discussions as they seek to position themselves ahead of their rivals.

Palmeiras are reportedly preparing for substantial offers, with some figures at the Brazilian club discussing a valuation as high as €100m (£85m).

Sources indicate that the player’s age is another consideration. Conceicao cannot complete an international transfer to England until he turns 18, leaving interested clubs facing a potentially lengthy wait before he can join their squads.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

Sources indicate that no formal bid or agreement has been reported for Conceicao. Nevertheless, the latest claims suggest Chelsea are prepared to explore another long-term investment in Brazilian talent rather than wait until the player becomes available for an immediate move.

Injured last Saturday in the 3-2 win at Nice (matchday 11 of Ligue 1), Desire Doue has suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and will be sidelined for around six months.

Above all, barring a miraculous recovery, the French right winger will not play again before the end of the 2026-27 season and will miss the spring fixtures, the Champions League first and foremost.

Since the announcement of the former Rennes man's injury, the question on everyone's mind is whether the capital club will use the winter transfer window to recruit.

While it could be argued that Paris have every interest in not signing anyone to replace Doue and Kvaratskhelia, the club's hierarchy may not share that view.

One certainty is that Paris Saint-Germain are monitoring several profiles ahead of January 2027. Among the names that keep coming up is that of versatile French forward Eli Junior Kroupi, for whom his club Bournemouth have set an astronomical price.

Although it would be surprising if the two-time reigning Champions League holders spent a fortune this winter, a cheaper option than the former Lorient man would interest the Ligue 1 leaders.

According to journalist Ekrem Konur, Paris Saint-Germain are eyeing Carlos Forbs. The young Portuguese right winger from Club Brugge is remarked to be one of the 'options being considered because of his versatility'. Arsenal have also opened a file on the player. Regarded as 'a more affordable solution' financially, the 22-year-old is having a very good 2026-27 season.

In 16 games in all competitions, Forbs has scored five goals and provided eight assists.

It has been revealed that in the Champions League, the former Manchester City youth player has made a splash with two goals and three assists in only four games. Lens still remember it: the Sintra-born winger scored one of the three goals in the Belgian side's 3-0 win over the French club on 21 October.

These top-level performances will no doubt encourage Club Brugge to keep him for another six months, although not without demanding a substantial sum given the current interest.

Under contract until June 2029, Forbs has a market value of £19.5m (€23m), which is well within reach for the coffers of these two European heavyweights. At least for now, but nothing says the Belgian hierarchy will let go easily once the battle begins.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Adrien Rabiot has had an outstanding start to the 2026-27 season, and he is showing absolutely no signs of slowing down.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report this morning by pointing out what Rabiot said after Milan’s 5-1 demolition of Frosinone on Sunday: “An assist is better than a goal.” He was the man of the match against Frosinone: five goals were scored, yet none bore his name.

Still, the Frenchman made himself the stand-out performer, thanks to his tireless running, leadership, and a series of decisive passes, not to mention his role in the opening goal, which came via an own-goal.

It has been revealed that it was a summer of doubts for Rabiot, given that his extended vacation was interpreted by some as a sign of discontent and a longing to reunite with his former mentor – Massimiliano Allegri – at Napoli. Yet, he has transformed into a cornerstone of this upcoming era.

According to recent reports, the former PSG man is now a decisive force on the pitch, integral to Ruben Amorim’s tactical framework, and a true leader. The numbers demonstrate this perfectly: Rabiot is the first midfielder to contribute to at least one goal (scoring or assisting) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004.

It has been revealed that with five goals and six assists, he recently became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A to record more than 10 goal contributions within the first 10 matches of a single season. In total, Rabiot has surpassed the milestone of 50 direct goal involvements in Serie A (29 goals and 22 assists).

Milan trust him, and the feeling is mutual. As previously mentioned, the very fact that he remained with the Rossoneri over the summer – publicly reaffirming his commitment to the club – is reflected in his attitude, both on and off the field.

Adrien Rabiot – Goal Contributions so far.

12 G/A in 14 Games https://t.co/s8oTle9GBn.

— c0mp (@c0mpmilano) November 23, 2026.

He is always smiling and highly active on social media; his numbers on Instagram are as impressive as his stats on the field. He posts photos of his goals, his celebrations and embraces with Diego Moreira, with whom he is clearly building a close bond.

Industry observers note that amorim noted after the game: “Adrien can play as a ’10,’ an attacking midfielder, an ‘8,’ or even as a playmaker – though he doesn’t particularly like that role. He is certainly one of the best players I have ever coached, and one of the best midfielders in Europe.”.

According to recent reports, speaking to Telefoot, Rabiot addressed the topic of his excellent start statistically: “It’s a positive thing to have players capable of being decisive, even if they aren’t forwards. It also serves as an encouragement to those around us.

Industry observers note that “At Milan, we have quite a few young players, and it’s vital for them to have role models in their day-to-day lives. I had only been back from vacation for a week when he was already talking to me about a contract renewal.

“I told him, ‘Coach, take it easy!’ (laughs). But, naturally, it’s significant for a player to feel that kind of trust—the coach relies on us, holds us in high regard, and makes us feel important.”.

Further significant remarks regarding Rabiot were made by Gerry Cardinale on the eve of the most recent league match, specifically concerning his imminent contract renewal.

“I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. He’s fantastic. I have enormous respect for him and his family. We are in talks, and I hope we reach a happy conclusion soon. I believe he should be a signature player for Milan. Could it be a Christmas gift for the fans? Absolutely, and for me, too.”.

The renewal will happen, and it will happen soon. Any delay until the fresh year should not be interpreted as a negative sign. Rather, it reflects the fact that everything is already settled, and there is no rush to finalise the signature.

Adrien’s current deal – which runs until 2028 – will be extended to 2030, with an additional one-year option. From his current age of 31, he will remain a fixture in the Rossoneri midfield until he is 33 or 34, the prime of his footballing maturity.

It has been revealed that now into his thirties, he will also earn a more lucrative contract than his current one, which pays him €3.5m net per season. It is worth noting that in the summer of 2025, Adrien was acquired from Marseille for €7m after a training-ground altercation with Jonathan Rowe.

It was, by any definition, a fantastic deal. As for the future, Rabiot has a role model he can observe from very close quarters: “Modrić trains as if he were 21, he’s an example to follow. The closer you get to the end of your career, the more you start to savor every moment. I try to do the same.”.

With the imminent contract extension, Adrien Rabiot is also set to conclude his career in the red and black colours, and that would make everyone happy.

Max Dowman has added another incredible achievement to his burgeoning career after becoming the youngest player to play for the England Under-21s.

Sources indicate that the Arsenal youngster was introduced from the bench in Friday’s 1-0 friendly loss to Portugal at Ashton Gate. The 16-year-10-month-13-day-old player is over three months younger than Jude Bellingham was when he played his first game for the Under-21s.

Industry observers note that dowman replaced former Arsenal academy player Amario Cozier-Duberry in the 61st minute. He came on alongside debutant Trey Nyoni as England tried to shift the momentum of a challenging game.

Dowman has added to his growing collection of records.

He became the youngest player to play in the Champions League, the youngest goalscorer in the history of the Premier League and the youngest to win the Premier League title.

Recent findings suggest that breaking Bellingham’s England Under-21 record is another significant step. It demonstrates how promptly Dowman has progressed through the international age groups.

He has already made a significant impression at Arsenal with Mikel Arteta’s love of giving younger players a chance, but Dowman will have some stiff competition for first team minutes.

Another positive is his progression on an international scale. He will improve both physically and tactically playing against older players and gain experience at a higher level.

England will host France in their next friendly on Monday, 16th November. Dowman will be hoping to feature after his instant impact on the record books.

Despite the disappointing result against Portugal, it was a landmark evening for the Arsenal players.

Dowman is already building a legacy at club level, but now he can add to his list of records by becoming an England Under-21 record holder.

At just 16, he has plenty of time to improve and show consistent performances to get more opportunities with the senior Arsenal squad.

Arsenal Women missed the chance to end their frustrating run of draws at home as London City Lionesses came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium.

Recent findings suggest that frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game. But Isobel Goodwin equalised almost straight away. Despite creating plenty of chances, Renée Slegers’ side failed to find a second goal.

Industry observers note that arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

According to recent reports, arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

Recent findings suggest that as the pressure mounted, Fox surged forward and played a perfectly weighted through ball to Alessia Russo. The striker turned and played the ball back to Maanum, who rounded off her impressive comeback from injury by finishing.

It has been revealed that arsenal had little time to rejoice. London City equalised just a minute later as Goodwin found herself in space to fire past Misa Rodríguez.

In a recent development, the visitors looked more confident after equalising, but Mary Earps was proving a tough ask for Arsenal to score past. The ex-Manchester United shot-stopper kept out Baum and made some key stops from Arsenal’s efforts.

Rodriguez also had to make a key stop before half-time as she got a hand to Daniela Arques Lazaro’s powerful strike to keep the scores level.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

But Arsenal still managed to create some chances. Caitlin Foord put Earps under pressure and Maanum and Baum combined before the latter saw her curl just wide.

Industry observers note that london City posed a threat too. With Kadidiatou Diani and Grace Geyoro causing defensive problems for Arsenal, Geyoro fired into the side netting.

Recent findings suggest that delphine Cascarino had the game’s defining moment of the second half, hitting the crossbar from outside the box. However, Arsenal were lucky to escape and Maanum came close to winning the game, hitting the woodwork from a dangerous counter.

Slegers brought on Kyra Cooney-Cross and Olivia Smith in the 72nd minute to provide some new energy. Smith looked lively upon entering the game, but Earps denied her efforts and Batlle’s cross.

Emily Fox had to be substituted due to injury in the final moments of the game, but Slegers later indicated that she would be okay.

According to recent reports, the Gunners were unable to find a winning goal and will now turn their attention to their Champions League clash on Thursday with Lyon. They will then face West Ham at home in the WSL.
