PSG transfer news: Spanish winger fits profile to cover Doue and Kvaratskhelia

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1062 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 06:57.
  • Paris Saint-Germain may have to turn to the transfer market to deal with a problem that threatens to change Luis Enrique's plans for the rest of the season.
  • According to recent reports, the injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue have left the manager without two of his main options on the flanks of the attack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 06:57.

Paris Saint-Germain may have to turn to the transfer market to deal with a problem that threatens to change Luis Enrique's plans for the rest of the season.

According to recent reports, the injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue have left the manager without two of his main options on the flanks of the attack. In that scenario, Athletic Bilbao's Nico Williams appears among the names being monitored by the French club, according to Le Parisien.

According to recent reports, at 24, the Spaniard combines speed, dribbling and the ability to play on both sides of the pitch. More than a replacement for the injured pair, he could offer Luis Enrique a characteristic that has become important to the team's attacking play: the ability to unbalance defences without depending on collective combinations.

Recent findings suggest that the importance of Kvaratskhelia and Doue to PSG is not limited to attacking output. Both offer mobility, the ability to carry the ball and the freedom to switch positions during matches. Their simultaneous absence forces Luis Enrique to find alternatives to maintain the unpredictability of a system based on constant movement.

Industry observers note that williams could help in that respect. His main characteristic is the ability to receive the ball wide and run at the full-back. His acceleration allows him to gain an advantage in a few metres. He also stands out for carrying the ball at speed and attacking both the outside channel and the space between full-back and centre-back.

That characteristic fits PSG's structure. Luis Enrique works with a team of fluid positions that nevertheless maintains reference points for occupying the pitch. When Kvaratskhelia moves from the left to occupy inside spaces, Nuno Mendes can advance and take over the width. The movement creates doubts for the opposition defence and allows the Georgian to take part more in build-up play from inside.

Industry observers note that williams could perform a similar dynamic, but with one difference: he tends to stay wider to receive the ball and exploit one-on-one duels. That would not be a problem, as it would give PSG an alternative for situations in which the opponent closes the central spaces and forces the team to find solutions down the flanks.

With the Spaniard wide, Nuno Mendes could better choose when to advance on the outside or take up inside positions. The presence of a winger capable of beating his marker without help would also open up space for runs from Vitinha, Joao Neves and the players who occupy the central area.

Williams also offers an notable quality in the final third: he can cross after beating the full-back, but also cut inside and find team-mates in the box. He is not just a sprinter who takes the ball to the byline. His ability to create for others was one of the hallmarks of Athletic's 2024 Copa del Rey campaign and of Spain's Euro 2024 campaign.

Signing Williams would not solve all of PSG's absences, because the three attackers have different characteristics. Kvaratskhelia is especially strong at carrying the ball in tight spaces and creating play from inside. Doue is more versatile, able to play on both sides and also in the middle, combining dribbling, physicality and creativity.

Williams is more vertical. He likes to receive the ball with space to accelerate and to turn seemingly controlled situations into individual duels. Rather than trying to reproduce exactly Kvaratskhelia's movements, he could offer a different way of attacking the same space.

According to recent reports, one of PSG's strengths lies in how the team changes its way of attacking depending on the opponent. With Williams, Paris could make more use of depth and duels down the flanks, especially against defences that push their lines up to press the French side's build-up.

Industry observers note that the Spaniard could also play on the right, although the left is his most natural position. That versatility would allow him to alternate sides with Mika Godts, as well as offering more possibilities for attacking rotations. There would be no need to tie Williams to a single flank.

Industry observers note that there is, however, one point to consider: Williams can still improve his decision-making and finishing efficiency. His game is heavily based on dribbling and acceleration, and the individual move does not always end in the best choice. At PSG, he would have to learn to balance personal initiative with the quick combinations that characterise Luis Enrique's model.

It has been revealed that if the tactical fit seems promising, the negotiation is more complicated. Williams renewed with Athletic in July 2025 until 2035, a move that ended, at least at that time, speculation over his departure to Barcelona.

The Basque club announced that the release clause had increased by more than 50 per cent compared with the previous contract. The Spanish press puts the figure at close to £76.5m (€90m).

In a recent development, the length of the contract gives Athletic enormous bargaining power. The club has no need to sell its main attacker and knows that PSG are looking for a solution to a problem created by injuries. If the French side really want the player, they will have to consider paying the clause in full or finding a deal that convinces the Basques.

According to recent reports, the player's own wishes also matter. Williams has publicly shown his attachment to Athletic and stated, on renewing, that he was where he wanted to be. A move to Paris could represent a sporting and financial leap, but his departure cannot be treated as automatic.

PSG, on the other hand, need to weigh up the length of the problem. The injuries to Doue and Kvaratskhelia are serious and should keep them out for much of the season, but the club does not necessarily need to sign two permanent replacements. The Le Parisien report stresses that the hierarchy has not yet decided whether it will go to the market and is also considering internal alternatives such as Senny Mayulu, Godts and Ferran Torres.

Williams would be an impact signing, able to solve an immediate need and remain key when the injured players return. But paying close to £76.5m for a player who was not necessarily in the plans before the injuries requires a very strong conviction.

After enduring the worst possible start to the 2026-27 campaign, during which Spurs failed to win any of their opening seven games, they have bounced back strongly in the league.

The north London club have picked up four wins in their last five matches, climbing to 10th in the Premier League table with 15 points, six adrift of fourth-placed Liverpool.

The 32-year-old midfielder is out of contract with the Italian giants at the end of the season, but preliminary talks have begun over an extension as he is keen to continue his career at San Siro.

Since joining from AC Milan in the summer of 2021, Calhanoglu has scored 53 goals in 226 appearances for the Nerazzurri.

The central midfielder registered 19 goal contributions in 30 games last term and has already scored three goals in his opening 10 league appearances this season.

While Spurs can match Calhanoglu's wage demands, they are not prepared to pay a transfer fee at this stage, instead hoping to sign him on a free transfer.

This leaves Tottenham anxiously waiting to see whether the Turkish midfielder can reach an agreement with Inter over a latest deal.

Calhanoglu can operate as a defensive midfielder and is renowned for his excellent long-range shooting, making him an exciting potential addition to De Zerbi's squad, even at this stage of his career.

  • Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

He was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

Storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

Storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

Storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

Sources indicate that he played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

It has been revealed that he will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

Published: 05:31 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 06:12 EST, 25 November 2026.

Rasmus Hojlund has laid bare the suffocating pressure of playing for Manchester United and given his insight into what Mauricio Pochettino’s squad will be suffering while marooned in the Premier League relegation zone.

The Dane was back in town this week after spending two seasons at United, mocking Manchester City fans when scoring the opener of Napoli’s 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night.

Hojlund secured a £38million permanent move away from Old Trafford in the summer but remains in touch with plenty of old team-mates and believes the lack of equilibrium at the club has contributed to a steady decline.

‘There are so many people following the club around the world and you can’t really escape from it,’ Hojlund said.

Industry observers note that ‘It is almost too high when it is good and almost too low when it is bad. It is all about trying to be in that middle. I had both the highs and the lows there.

‘The pressure is part of the club, it comes with playing for United. There has been a lot of change but hopefully they will get it right with Mauricio.’.

Rasmus Hojlund mocked Man City fans after scoring for Napoli at the Etihad on Tuesday night.

A United supporter, Hojlund laughed off the idea that the club is in a relegation scrap despite their worst start to a season since 1972. And the 23-year-old revealed that the players were ready for ‘change’ following the sacking of Michael Carrick.

‘I spoke with Bruno [Fernandes] and Diogo [Dalot] during the international break and they were all obviously devastated that Michael was going but also looking forward to some change,’ Hojlund added.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I am still speaking with Patrick [Dorgu] and I just wish the guys all the best. I am sure they will turn it around this season. They have got a lot of quality. They have got a great squad, good leaders, good professionals.

‘It is a temporary picture, I think they will get back to the top. The Premier League is like this. I read the other day that Bournemouth was in the relegation zone after a couple of games, now they have won the last five games and are in the top half of the table.’.

With the club at something of an all time low in the modern era, mid table in the second division being their lowest standing in living memory, critics are lining up to have a pop at events on and off the pitch.

Head of Recruitment Nils Koppen does not escape.

His marquee signing of Arne Engels has come upper fire from several sources. The Belgian midfielder actually didn’t have too bad a game – by comparison – against Portsmouth, but that hasn’t stopped many from pointing the finger at West Ham’s summer signing,  with Talk SPORT’s Tom Rennie (Reported with glee by the glasgowtimes.co.uk) apparently leading the charge:.

Sources indicate that I just don’t see one thing Engels does that James Ward-Prowse couldn’t do,” [Rennie said]. “.

That £22m could have been spent on RB, CB, LW, GK. Koppen can’t be allowed another transfer window.”.

I’d have to beg to differ, Engels’ through ball that set up Piroe against Preston North End was pure Paquetá in his pomp.

According to recent reports, ward Prowse could only move the ball sideways and backwards. In addition I remember one notorious foot race between Ward Prowse and an opposition goal keeper which the ‘keeper won comfortably, leaving JWP for dead over 40 yards.

In a recent development, true enough, Engels may not be the finished article. But he’s more combative in the tackle, faster across the turf and he has been known to pass the ball forwards. A little like Mateus Fernandez, he’ll likely grow into the season and become undroppable by May.

There are plenty in this West Ham side who are not worth their starting spot or their wages but I’d not put Engels even close to the front of that particular list.

Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5228 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics.

Recent findings suggest that a, High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) image of the NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbon with Nb (3.4 nm) seed layer. The electrically-conducting width of this device is ~12.5 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed, together with their corresponding Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), obtained from the boxed regions in panel a. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions. In total, three NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbons were examined by cross-sectional STEM. Across these samples, we observe consistent structural and compositional characteristics, including similar NbP crystallinity and sidewall oxidation, which support the scaling behaviour reported in this work. Additional STEM characterization was not performed on thicker NbP nanoribbons, as the thinnest nanoribbons are most relevant to the main conclusions of this study.

a, HAADF image of the NbP (1.5 nm)/Nb (3.4 nm) nanoribbon with an electrically-conducting width of ~18 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed layer, together with their corresponding FFT, obtained from the boxed regions. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and EDS elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions of each region. e, EELS linescan profiles of Nb (blue) and P (red) normalized intensity as a function of position along the direction indicated in panel c. f-h, Representative nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) patterns extracted from 4D-STEM data at probe positions within the sapphire substrate (f), Nb layer (g), and NbP layer (h), with indexed reflections confirming the distinct crystal structure of each region. i-k, Orientation template matching of the representative NBED pattern in f–h, for the sapphire substrate (i), Nb layer (j) and NbP layer (k). Coloured symbols indicate the local crystallographic orientation of the best-matching template for that pattern. l-n, Phase template matching of the same patterns for the sapphire substrate (l), Nb layer (m) and NbP layer (n).

a, Schematic of the scaling mechanism for conventional metals, with surface scattering and grain boundary scattering. b, As thickness and width of NbP are reduced, the conduction is consistent with the growing dominance of surface carriers, which are disorder-tolerant, with reduced scattering. The total sheet conductance in this case is a sum of the sheet conductance contributed from bulk carriers and surface carriers. c, For thick NbP, bulk carriers dominate the transport, and thus conventional scaling laws apply, with pronounced surface and grain boundary scattering. d, The Fuchs-Sondheimer (FS) and Mayadas-Shatzkes (MS) model fitting of 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, showing an excellent fit. The extracted resistivity with increasing width (W → ∞) is 56.3 μΩ∙cm, which matches the literature results. e, Sheet conductance (GNbP,□) of 1.5 nm NbP as a function of width (red curve), extracted from Fig. 2d of the main text. The sheet conductance from bulk carriers (extracted from Hall measurement) follows the conventional FS-MS scaling model (black dashed line), where the sheet conductance from surface carriers increases as the width decreases due to the increased surface area/volume ratio, as indicated by the purple dashed line. At this ultrathin thickness (1.5 nm), bulk carriers experience strong scattering, resulting in very small bulk carrier sheet conductance. f, GNbP,□ of 10 nm NbP as a function of width (blue curve). At NbP thickness of 10 nm, 3D bulk carriers and 2D top and bottom surface carriers contribute comparably to transport, as shown in Fig. 4b. At this thickness, as the nanoribbon width is reduced, the enhancement in surface conduction is insufficient to offset the increased scattering of bulk carriers. Consequently, bulk transport dominates in this regime, leading to a net reduction of sheet conductance (i.e., increased resistivity) with decreasing width, more similar to conventional metal wires. We note that there could be subtle differences in sidewall roughness and damage in the thicker nanoribbons compared to the thinner ones. See Supplementary Note 2 for the modelling details and more discussion.

It has been revealed that a, Bulk Brillouin-zone schematic showing the two mirror planes and nodal rings from the band inversion. b, Representative band dispersion along Γ-S-M’, where the curves calculated without spin-orbit coupling (SOC) show the nodal-ring-related band inversion (plotted in green), and the curves calculated with SOC show the corresponding gap opening (black dashed lines). c, Real-space crystal view highlighting the helical states along the projected mirror line on the surface. d, Surface-state spectrum along \(\overline{\Gamma }\)-\(\overline{{\rm{X}}}\)-\(\overline{\Gamma }\)’, where the narrow Weyl-point window (grey shadow) hosts three pairs of helical states (indicated by arrows) that form the main part of the Fermi arcs, while remnant spin-split surface branches remain visible over a broader energy window (broad green shadow). Blue and red colours indicate the ‘± Sy’ spin polarization at opposite momenta, showing the helical feature. In summary, the narrow Fermi-arc structure is embedded inside a much broader nodal-ring-derived surface-state sector set by the band inversion. See Supplementary Note 7 for more discussion on bulk-topology hierarchy and topological surface-state interpretation.

a, Slab model along the [001] direction for the surface state calculations. Here, the 2 × 2 × 3 supercell is shown as an example. A 4.5 nm thick slab structure of the 1 × 1 × 4 supercell was used in the calculations. b,c, Surface band structures with Nb (b) and P (c) terminations along high-symmetry lines. Blue and red bands indicate the surface states of the Nb and P terminations, respectively. Bulk-projected states shown in pale blue are depicted as the background. The charge neutral point is set to 0 eV. d-f, Surface-projected Fermi surfaces with Nb (upper panels) and P (lower panels) terminations at 0 eV (d), −0.2 eV (e), and −0.4 eV (f). Darker colours represent larger contributions projected from the surface. Weyl points projected on the 2D Brillouin zone are shown as green and purple dots for opposite chirality. The constant energy cuts show surface-dominant open contours over a broad energy window, indicating that Weyl-derived surface bands persist even when the chemical potential is shifted deep into the hole-doped regime, which implies the robustness of the topological surface character. In addition, for the 4.5 nm thick NbP film, the top and bottom surface states exhibit minimal hybridization, except near the Weyl point projections where they meet each other. The Fermi-arc states remain largely unhybridized because they are well separated in momentum space. Even at momenta where they intersect, the resulting hybridization gap is negligible. See Supplementary Note 8 for the modelling details and more discussion.

a, Slab model from the NbP (001) film with thickness d = 1.5 nm and width W = 4.4 to 5.7 nm. b, The one-dimensional (1D) band structure of a W = 5 nm nanoribbon along ky direction. The edge projection is highlighted in purple to show the edge states, while the bulk states are shown in pale blue. Near EF, the edge-projected subbands form an electron-like pocket, consistent with the negative pedge values (panel f). c-e, The spin projection to Sx (c), Sy (d), and Sz (e) components, respectively, for the edge state. The blue and red represent opposite signs of spin polarization. These edge states exhibit a pronounced spin texture arising from strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in noncentrosymmetric NbP where Sx and Sz components are locked to the ky momentum in a Rashba-type SOC. This reduces the wavefunction overlap between counter-propagating modes, thereby suppressing the leading backscattering channel, which indicates high-mobility edge conduction. f, The carrier densities from edge (pedge) and 2D film (p2D) are extracted from linear fitting of the total ribbon density (p1D) by p1D = pedge + p2DW, at varying W. Wc denotes the cross-over width at which the edge carrier density would dominate the transport over the top and bottom surface carrier density. Here, Wc ≈ 0 indicates that the enhanced edge conduction of ultrathin films is not primarily driven by an increased edge carrier density. Instead, it is more plausibly attributed to an enhanced carrier mobility arising from reduced backscattering as the edge dimension approaches the quasi-1D limit. See more details in Supplementary Notes 2 and 8. g, Agreement between the nanoribbon fitting (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{NR}}}\)) and that obtained from independent slab film calculations (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{slab}}}\)) which corresponds to the d = 1.5 nm thickness in Supplementary Fig. 10. This agreement supports the self-consistency of our calculations across both the nanoribbon and thin-film geometries.

a, Temperature-dependent effective resistivity (ρeff) of NbP films with different thicknesses up to 90 nm, measured from Hall bar devices. These films have a 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, whose resistivity is measured separately (black symbols). b, Low-temperature limit (2-10 K) of panel a. The smallest superconducting transition temperature Tc (~2.2 K) is in the 3.4 nm Nb layer (black symbols), while higher Tc are observed in the NbP/Nb films, and Tc decreases monotonically with thicker NbP. The symbol colours follow the convention in panel a. c,d, Temperature-dependent sheet conductance (GNbP,□) (c) and resistivity (ρNbP) (d) for all NbP thicknesses, after subtracting the Nb seed contribution. e, ρNbP as a function of NbP thickness at 300 K and 10 K. For comparison, the ρNbP values of nanoribbons with the widest widths (Fig. 2d of the main text) are slightly higher than those from Hall measurements at 300 K, possibly due to process-induced damage during nanofabrication. f, Temperature-dependent ρeff of a ~5 nm-thick Nb control film, measured from a Hall bar device. The residual resistivity ratio (RRR) is 1.48, and the Tc is ~4.2 K. Inset: enlarged view of the low-temperature region. The presence of NbP appears to promote superconductivity in NbP/Nb films. The superconducting proximity effect is one plausible interpretation, although changes in disorder and enhanced inter-grain coupling (in the presence of NbP layer) could also contribute. We also cannot fully rule out the formation of an interfacial superconducting layer at the NbP/Nb interface. The NbP sheet conductance is obtained by subtracting the sheet conductance of the Nb layer (measured independently on control Nb films) from the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack. The extracted NbP resistivity is then obtained by dividing the NbP thickness by the NbP sheet conductance, i.e. ρNbP = dNbP/GNbP,□, where GNbP,□ = Gtot,□ - GNb,□ and Gtot,□ = dtot/ρeff, where Gtot,□ is the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack, dtot is the total stack thickness and ρeff is the measured effective resistivity (panel a). The GNbP,□ (panel c) represents the NbP sheet conductance after subtracting the independently-measured Nb seed contribution. Additional validation of the subtraction method using Pt/Nb stacks is provided in Supplementary Fig. 19. Control experiments using Pt/Nb stacks validate that the subtraction procedure itself does not generate an anomalous resistivity trend. Nevertheless, the conductance of the Nb seed layer within NbP/Nb stacks cannot be independently measured and it cannot be remarked, with absolute certainty, that its behaviour is identical to that of the separately measured Nb control film. Thus, the extracted NbP resistivity relies, by necessity, on the model used.

a-c, Hall resistance (Rxy) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for 3.4 nm Nb (a), 1.5 nm NbP (b), and 10 nm NbP (c). For the NbP films (b,c), the Nb seed layer contribution is subtracted at each corresponding temperature to extract NbP Hall response, using the same two-layer Hall conduction model described in the supplement. d, Effective three-dimensional carrier density (p3D) for all films, revealing opposite temperature-dependence: ultrathin 1.5 nm NbP reveals an increasing p3D upon cooling, whereas both thicker NbP (10 nm) and Nb (3.4 nm) display decreasing p3D. (This figure is also included in the main text as Fig. 4d and is reproduced here for convenience). e, Effective hole mobility (μp) of the same films vs. temperature. NbP films exhibit a pronounced increase in mobility upon cooling due to suppressed phonon scattering, whereas the 3.4 nm Nb film shows only a slight rise in mobility, indicating that its transport remains strongly limited by surface scattering.

It has been revealed that a-c, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for films of Nb seed layer (3.4 nm) (a), for NbP (1.5 nm) on the Nb seed (b), and for NbP (10 nm) on the Nb seed (c). All measurements were performed with the magnetic field applied perpendicular to the film plane and current direction. At low temperatures, all films exhibit a pronounced negative cusp near low field regions, arising from the interplay of superconducting fluctuations and weak antilocalization. d-e, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at 1.8 K for both 1.5 nm thick NbP (on 3.4 nm Nb seed layer) and for the Nb layer (3.4 nm) evaluated separately. Measurements were performed with B field perpendicular to the film plane and current direction (d), and with B applied in-plane (e). The superconducting transition temperatures are Tc ~ 6 K for the 1.5 nm NbP (on Nb) and ~2.2 K for the 3.4 nm Nb film (see Fig. 3d of the main text). The upper critical field Hc2, defined as the midpoint between the normal state resistance and zero resistance, is extracted. At 1.8 K, the out-of-plane critical field \({H}_{c2}^{\perp }\) is 2.2 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and 0.38 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The in-plane critical field at 1.8 K exceeds 9 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and reaches 4.44 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The superconducting coherence length estimates are provided in the supplement. The sense current used for Hall bar measurements is 0.5 mA, corresponding to a current density of ~0.1 MA/cm2 for the NbP (1.5 nm) film and ~0.15 MA/cm2 for the 3.4 nm Nb control, with the same 100 μm Hall bar device width. We note that this sense current is well below the superconducting critical current: even when we increased the sense current up to 10 mA, we were unable to suppress the superconducting state at 1.8 K.

It has been revealed that a, Cross-sectional HAADF STEM image of the alternating NbP/Nb multilayers grown on sapphire. b-d, Denoised nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) patterns extracted from 4D-STEM data for all Nb layers (Nb layers 1-3) showing consistent body-centred cubic (bcc) diffraction symmetry with indexed reflections, confirming crystalline quality across all Nb layers. Scale bars: 0.5 Å−1. e, EDS line scan across the multilayer stack showing Nb (blue), P (red), and Al (light brown) as a function of position, integrated over a ~ 5nm wide region along the direction indicated by the yellow arrow in panel a, confirming periodic composition and abrupt elemental transitions at each NbP/Nb interface. f-h, denoised NBED patterns from NbP layers 1–3, displaying diffraction symmetry consistent with the NbP crystal structure with indexed reflections, consistent with uniform phase and crystallographic orientation throughout the multilayer stack. The diffraction spots become progressively broader from layer 1 to layer 3, suggesting a gradual decrease in crystalline coherence in NbP layers further from the substrate. This is further supported by the emergence of diffuse ring features in the Layer 3 diffraction pattern, indicative of increasing structural disorder.

Christos Tzolis challenges Arsenal critics with a message about his physicality

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Winger Christos Tzolis wants to prove he has a lot to offer Arsenal beyond his attacking prowess.

In a recent development, since moving to the club from Club Brugge in July, the 24-year-old has made a great start to life at the club after an impressive season in Belgium. The Greek attacker scored 17 goals and made 23 assists in 36 league games.

Recent findings suggest that but doubts were raised about his ease of integration into the Premier League. In his first stint in England with Norwich City, he showed little sign of becoming the player he is now.

According to recent reports, since making his debut for the club, Tzolis has become a more rounded attacking threat. He has started all 7 Premier League games this season and provides a reliable option on the left for Arteta.

However, in recent comments, it seems that he is aware of the perceptions around his physicality and is keen to change them.

Tzolis spoke to Arsenal Media, saying that he doesn’t think the notion of him lacking the physicality to play at top level has validity.

He claimed that he is not a player without muscle and cited his accomplishments. He also described his tendency to use aggression against his opponents.

In a recent development, this is a key part of Arteta’s system at the club. Tzolis is expected to press from the flanks if Arsenal lose the ball.

Tzolis is comfortable with this role. He is able to track back well to support his full-back, adding an extra dimension to the left side.

The Greek international has proven his physical ability outside of match play. He was nicknamed Leonidas by the fitness team at the club due to a strong performance in pre-season.

It is reported that he completed the running challenge better than anyone in the squad.

Recent findings suggest that tzolis has joined Arsenal to add attacking flair to the squad, having left for Besiktas. He looks like he could be a formidable goalscorer and creator.

Recent findings suggest that in the league last season, Tzolis contributed 40 goals and put in a good performance in Europe. This led to Arsenal spending a reported £34 million to bring him to the club.

He has not had the best impact in the league, registering just one assist and no goals, but this should not be taken to mean he is not contributing.

In a recent development, tzolis has shown an ability to fit into Arteta’s style of play. His defensive contribution, work rate and combative nature may prove very valuable in tough away games.

Despite there being plenty to improve on, Tzolis provides more than just an attacking option for Arsenal.

If Tzolis can change people’s view of him in terms of his physicality and continues to put his technical skills and determination together, then he can be a valuable asset in Arteta’s plans.

Man Utd transfer stance on Marcus Rashford 'revealed' after Mauricio Pochettino's arrival

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 26 Nov 2026 08:21.
  • Manchester United reportedly remain open to selling Marcus Rashford in January if they receive a suitable offer for the forward.
  • Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona, and it appeared that his future lay away from Old Trafford after he fell out with former manager Ruben Amorim.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 26 Nov 2026 08:21.

Manchester United reportedly remain open to selling Marcus Rashford in January if they receive a suitable offer for the forward.

Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona, and it appeared that his future lay away from Old Trafford after he fell out with former manager Ruben Amorim.

Man Utd publicly backed his reintegration into the squad after Barcelona opted against signing him permanently, but the England international has so far cut a disappointing figure.

Rashford has made six Premier League appearances this season, starting four of them, but is yet to register a goal or assist.

With Mauricio Pochettino looking to reshape the attacking line-up in his own image, Rashford could once again find himself facing an uncertain future.

Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, transfer expert Ben Jacobs has suggested that the Red Devils would still consider suitable offers for Rashford.

The forward remains under contract at United until 2028, meaning the club are under no immediate pressure to sell him.

At the same time, the Red Devils could consider letting him leave as they look to add depth and quality to their forward department in January or potentially next summer.

Rashford is right now sidelined with a hip injury and missed both of Pochettino's first two games in charge. However, the club expect him to return before the end of the month, potentially in time for the clash against Brentford.

Joshua Zirkzee came on at half-time against Liverpool, but there is a strong possibility that the Dutch striker could be offloaded, with several Serie A clubs reportedly keen on his signature.

Pochettino also needs to reshape his defence, with signing a new centre-back a priority, potentially putting Lisandro Martinez's future at the club in doubt.

There are also doubts over the long-term future of captain Bruno Fernandes, who has already rejected two contract offers from the club.
